# Claude Task Plan

This document is the master reference consumed by Claude remote routines. Each routine's instruction is the single line:

> Read Claude_Task_Plan.md. Perform <task ID> — <deep research | regular routine>.

**ROUTINE SLICE ROUTING.** Execute routine `<ID>` from `task_plan/<ID>.md` (generated from this monolith and CI byte-checked). If you are already reading that slice, you are in the right place. Open another routine's slice only when hosting that routine or following a cross-reference to it (for example, OPS2 hosting W5/SL1). Make plan edits only in `Claude_Task_Plan.md`, then regenerate with `python3 scripts/split_task_plan.py`; never edit generated slices directly. If the slice is missing, fall back to this monolith.

Claude reads this file at the start of every routine run, locates the matching `## <ID>. ...` section, and executes the prompt body inside that section. Section IDs (D1, D2, W1, ..., A3) are stable; routine names mirror them. (Generic form since 2026-08-17 — the trigger's live instruction carries only the id + type tag, not the description clause, so a routine RENAME never needs a live `RemoteTrigger update` push for the instruction half; the description lives only in the trigger's `name` field and this file's `## <ID>. <description> — <type>` heading. AR_att/AR_orc have no coded id prefix, so their full heading is the instruction verbatim, unchanged.)

# ROUTINE INVENTORY & BIGQUERY RESPONSIBILITIES

Every routine reads and/or writes BigQuery for operational state (positions, regime, decisions, queues, NAV, perf/kill-flags, macro). **Therefore every routine MUST have the Google Cloud BigQuery connector enabled** — without it the routine cannot find the state it needs and fails on restart. This is the single-page map of each routine's BigQuery I/O, derived from each routine's prompt body **plus the Operating_Protocols.md §15 authoritative-source override** (which redirects the retired `.md` reads/writes: Regime_State → `state.current_regime`; Portfolio_Ledger → `state.current_positions` / `perf.strategy_daily` / `analytics.strategy_nav` / `analytics.account_reconciliation`; Decision_Log → `events.decision_log` / `find_precedents()`; the `Pending_*` queues → `state.open_queue` / `events.queue_events`). The action-conversion routines (D2 / M4 / Q4 / A3) and W4's queue-only research handoff are the primary BigQuery writers; deep-research routines mainly read state and write their cadence `.md` output (last column).

# OPERATING MODEL

## Execution environment

Claude runs as scheduled routines connected to a GitHub repo (currently `JackOfSpade/Stock-Trading`) and to Google Calendar via MCP. Inside a routine Claude has:

- **BigQuery (Google Cloud MCP connector) — the canonical operational data substrate (project `stock-trading-498512`).** All migrated state/history lives in BigQuery, NOT repo `.md`: positions/fills/marks (`events.*` → `state.current_positions`, `perf.strategy_daily`, `perf.kill_flags`), decisions (`events.decision_log`, `analytics.find_precedents()`), regime/router (`state.current_regime`), queues (`state.open_queue`, `events.queue_events`), NAV/2%-sizing base (`analytics.strategy_nav`), §13 reconciliation (`analytics.account_reconciliation`), calibration (`analytics.calibration_summary`), macro (`events.macro_series`), consolidated `state.daily_briefing`. READ via `execute_sql_readonly`; WRITE via `execute_sql`. **Every routine MUST have the Google Cloud BigQuery connector enabled**. Source map/read-write override: Operating_Protocols.md §14–15.
- **Repo `.md` files (read/write) — now SPEC + cadence-working files only.** Read spec/rules files (Strategy.md, Experiment_Parameters.md, Operating_Protocols.md, Claude_Task_Plan.md, AI_Trading_Foundation.md, B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md, C/E methodology docs, HF_Resource_Catalog.md); edit only for protocol/spec changes. Overwrite/edit cadence outputs (Daily.md, Weekly_*.md, Monthly_*.md, Quarterly_*.md, Annual_*.md) and Strategy-A Watchlist.md per run. Decision_Log, Portfolio_Ledger, Regime_State, Pending_* and all former archives are **RETIRED — read/write BigQuery instead** (§15).
- **Calendar MCP** — only non-craftable/manual-entry orders and BigQuery-unreachable pre-flight (Calendar MCP usage below). Claude-only analysis runs in-session or in `PENDING_ANALYSIS` (`state.open_queue` / `events.queue_events`, D2 drains daily), NEVER on the calendar; structured adversarial reviews use `PENDING_REVIEW` (ADVERSARIAL REVIEWS).
- **IBKR connector (MCP)** — authenticated live account/market data and tap-confirm orders: `create_order_instruction` → deep link; account reads `get_account_summary` / `get_account_positions` / `get_account_balances` / `get_account_orders` / `get_account_trades`; market reads `get_price_snapshot` / `get_price_history` / `search_contracts`. Read fills/positions/cash directly; craft Equity/ETF, single-leg Options and OPT–OPT combos/spreads, with manual text fallback only for mixed-type/FOP combos. Protocol: Operating_Protocols.md §11 and IBKR connector usage below.
- **Web research tools** (Tavily, web_search, web_fetch) for deep-research cadences. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-01.)*

Each routine run is a fresh session — there is no cross-run chat memory. State persists only in repo files and calendar events. Every prompt body in this document is therefore self-contained: it specifies which repo files to read, which to write, and which calendar events to create.

**GIT HISTORY IS TRUNCATED IN THE ROUTINE CONTAINER — RUN THE HISTORY-DEPTH PRECHECK BEFORE ANY CLAIM ABOUT WHO CHANGED SOMETHING, OR WHEN (added 2026-09-08; hoisted fleet-wide from OPS0 STEP 4(a) after SL2 raised `shallow_clone_git_attribution` at `warning`, correctly reporting that the exposure is EVERY routine's and its own pin reached only SL2).** The container clones this repo **SHALLOW**. Measured twice, independently, by two different routines: 2026-08-03 by OPS0 (boundary `f5bbade`, **65** commits reachable from `origin/main`, **972** after `--unshallow`) and 2026-09-08 by SL2 (boundary `e4e611c` dated 2026-09-01, **83** commits). Both boundaries sit roughly a week back, so the truncation is time-bounded rather than a fixed depth — it slides forward with the calendar, and "history was fine when I checked last week" is not evidence about today.

- **THE FAILURE MODE IS A WRONG ANSWER, NEVER AN ERROR — which is the whole reason this needs a rule.** Truncated-history `git log -S`/`-G`, `git log -L`, `git blame`, `git log --follow`, `git log --since`/`--until`, `git rev-list --count`, `git describe` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` can exit 0 while attributing pre-boundary changes to the boundary; `--- /dev/null` does not prove creation there.
- **A DEEPEN NOW RUNS BEFORE YOUR FIRST TOOL CALL, SO THE USUAL STATE IS COMPLETE — AND YOU STILL ASK, BECAUSE IT IS BEST-EFFORT.** `.claude/session-start.sh` runs `git fetch --unshallow origin` only on a shallow clone; failure warns but never blocks, so still run the precheck.
- **THE HISTORY-DEPTH PRECHECK — three steps, in this order, before the FIRST history-reasoning command of any run that will assert an authorship, an "introduced in", a "has not changed since", or an ancestry verdict.** **1. ASK:** `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`; if `false`, skip step 2 and proceed. **2. DEEPEN only if `true`:** `git fetch --unshallow origin`. **3. RE-ASK:** `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`; `false` proves completeness. Do not collapse these steps: `fatal: --unshallow on a complete repository does not make sense` proves the clone is COMPLETE, so proceed rather than taking the skip path.
- **UNDEEPENABLE (step 3 still prints `true`) → every history answer this run is INCONCLUSIVE, never a finding.** Never write attribution, introduction/unchanged-since or non-ancestor verdicts into `events.decision_log`, `ops.alerts`, pinned rules, cadence `.md` or `<note>` from truncated evidence; write `history truncated at <boundary>; attribution not established this run` and leave the question open. Apply each routine's own undeepenable consequences, especially OPS0 STEP 4; State provenance applies.
- **THE TELL, for a session that has already reasoned before reading this.** Independent `-S`/`-L`/`blame` probes landing on one commit, or `--- /dev/null` for a known-older file, require step 1 before recording a conclusion. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-02.)*

- **THE LOCAL TEST SUITE IS UNRUNNABLE IN THE ROUTINE CONTAINER AS IMAGED — AN ENVIRONMENT GAP THAT PRESENTS AS A REPOSITORY DEFECT.** Missing `requirements-ci.txt` dependencies make `python -m pytest tests/` abort at collection via `scripts/apply_sql_file.py`'s `google.cloud.bigquery` guard; do not diagnose this as a broken suite or your change. Use `pip install --ignore-installed -r requirements-ci.txt`: plain install fails on Debian's `packaging` RECORD. This changes no repo file. `pyproject.toml` already adds `-q`; another `-q` suppresses pytest 8.4.2's summary, so exit 0 proves completion. Use `pytest tests/` without another verbosity flag for a summary. CI is authoritative for a landed commit; local tests corroborate it.

## Branch and state propagation

Routines work only on the harness-assigned `claude/<suffix>` branch. They autonomously commit and push their OWN assigned branch, open or reuse its same-repository PR targeting `main`, wait for its exact current head's required checks, and explicitly invoke `.github/workflows/auto-merge-claude.yml` with that PR number. This **Merge validated PR** workflow merges only that selected, validated PR and preserves the landed routine markers. There is no human approval step in the scheduled routine publication path. Never push directly to `main`, bypass branch protection, enumerate branches for merging, delete branches, or adopt another session's work without explicit owner selection.

**Why.** The harness permits pushes only to its assigned `claude/<suffix>` branch; GitHub checks precede the selected workflow's server-side merge. This grants no shell authorization: if `gh` or existing repo/workflow permission is unavailable, leave the pushed branch and PR intact, record publication as unconfirmed and report the blocker. Never substitute a direct-main push, administrator override, another branch's credentials or a human approval requirement for an authorized routine.

**Session start.** `.claude/settings.json` runs `.claude/session-start.sh`: `git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main`, staying on the assigned branch. It best-effort deepens shallow clones with `git fetch --unshallow origin`, guarded by `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`; failure warns on stderr without blocking. `tests/test_session_start_hook.sh` pins shallow deepen, no unshallow on complete clones, and warning on failure. Run the §Execution environment **HISTORY-DEPTH PRECHECK** before attribution even after this hook. Read BigQuery operational state and working/spec `.md` inputs after the hook.

**During the routine.** Edit normally on the assigned branch and run the applicable local gates. Regenerate generated files with their checked-in generators. Do not switch to `main`, push to it, modify another session's branch, or treat an existing unrelated PR as this routine's publication. Opening the routine's OWN PR is required for repo output; the former “Do not open PRs” instruction and push-triggered branch drain are retired.

**Session end — explicit own-PR publication.** (1) Commit output, SUBJECT starts **`<ROUTINE> <YYYY-MM-DD>: `** (routine id + Denver run date; OPS2-hosted work uses the HOSTED id); halt records instead use RUNBOOK §48. Only SUBJECT drives `scripts/write_routine_commit_markers.sh`/`marker_routine_from_subject`, §38 self-heal and OPS0 STEP 4(f). Explicitly `git push -u origin <assigned-branch>`; verify `git ls-remote --exit-code origin refs/heads/<assigned-branch>` equals local `HEAD`, up to three total attempts (~5s, then ~15s backoff). (2) Reuse an OPEN PR ONLY for this repo/exact assigned head branch/base `main`; else create, e.g. `gh pr create --base main --head <assigned-branch> --title '<ROUTINE> <YYYY-MM-DD>: <summary>' --body '<output and validation>'`. Record number/exact head SHA; never select by title/age/first result. (3) Fetch main; require ancestor of PR head. If advanced, merge `origin/main` into ONLY assigned branch, resolve only unambiguous conflicts, regenerate slices/rerun gates/push without force/restart verification; preserve branch/PR and report ambiguous conflicts. (4) At that exact head require the LATEST results for **`CI required`, `Security required`, `Dependency review required`, and native `CodeQL`** all to complete successfully; inspect SHA-specific check-runs/statuses, verify the three named workflow checks originate from GitHub Actions, and include native code scanning even if `gh pr checks --required` omits it. Old/other-SHA/pending/missing/skipped/cancelled checks fail. Re-read head/main before dispatch; changes restart ancestry/checks. Repair content failure on OWN branch/new checked head; never blindly rerun deterministic failure. (5) Dispatch exactly `gh workflow run auto-merge-claude.yml --repo JackOfSpade/Stock-Trading --ref main -f pr_number=<selected-number>`; no branch sweep. After confirmed merge the workflow deletes only this PR's branch while it still names the merged head. (6) Poll selected PR/fetch main: require GitHub `merged=true`, recorded `merge_commit_sha` AND checked head ancestral to `origin/main`. Dispatch acceptance is not receipt; stale-main/head/check rejection restarts own-branch path. Wait within session time; timeout preserves PR and reports URL/SHA/outstanding checks/landing status. Repo-output completion requires confirmed main landing. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-04.)*

**A ZERO-REPO-DIFF RUN PUSHES NOTHING, AND ITS `completed` IS NOT THEREBY UNGATED — SAY SO IN `<note>` (added 2026-09-21, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing AR_att's `session_end_push_unstated_for_zero_diff_run`, alert `0b660d32-9e31-4c99-91df-9e15fdacbd2a`).** Working tree clean AND `HEAD == origin/main` AND no commit made this run: push nothing, create no remote branch, log `completed` with one affirmative `<note>` line, e.g. `REPO OUTPUT: NONE. Working tree clean at <sha>, equal to origin/main; no commit made, so no push is owed and the verified-push gate is satisfied vacuously, not skipped.` ANY commit made this run, including one prose file, instead requires the full own-PR protocol and confirmed main landing before `completed`; judge by the commit, never a perceived no-op. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-05.)*

**REGENERATE THE GENERATED SLICES IN THE SAME COMMIT THAT EDITS THEIR MASTER — `Claude_Task_Plan.md` → `scripts/split_task_plan.py`, `Strategy.md` → `scripts/split_strategy.py`.** After ANY master edit run its generator, stage output and run `--check` before pushing; repair stale-slice CI failures on the OWN assigned branch during this session. Do not rely on implicit session-end push or the retired one-rerun branch drain. **CHECKPOINT PUSHES — targeted, not blanket.** Checkpoint (a) before bounded TRANSIENT-FAILURE WAIT-AND-RETRY or DEPENDENCY-WAIT windows that may outlive the container, (b) deep-research routines immediately after primary output (`ops/triggers.json`'s `— deep research.` instructions govern); others publish once per completed unit. Checkpoints use exact-SHA `ls-remote` verification, never gate `sp_routine_end` or merge unfinished work; note failure and finish own-PR publication when ready. Repo-output `completed` requires confirmed main landing. After three failed push verifications, use `error_msg='branch push unconfirmed after 3 verification attempts — output may be stranded'` and `'failed'`/`'halted'`; unconfirmed checks/merge/ancestry likewise use `'failed'`/`'halted'`, specific blocker and PR URL. Preserve already-performed BigQuery effects/idempotency markers; do not repeat or roll them back for publication failure, and report them separately. SessionStart reads confirmed main only.

**NAMING A NEW `mcp__*` TOOL IN ROUTINE PROSE REQUIRES THE MANIFEST *AND* THE ALLOWLIST IN THE SAME COMMIT (added 2026-08-30, after this stranded D1's 2026-08-30 run).** Every added/changed `mcp__<Connector>__<tool>` in `Claude_Task_Plan.md` requires (1) `ops/connector_tools.yaml` `use: required` (CHECK3 rejects `unused`/`optional`), (2) `.claude/settings.json` `permissions.allow` entry `<settings_prefix><tool>` (CHECK2/toolcov). Run blocking `python scripts/check_connector_tools.py` and `python scripts/check_settings_toolcov.py` before pushing. Both scan the plan; toolcov also scans `ops/triggers.json`; neither scans `Operating_Protocols.md`, `Strategy.md`, `strategy/**` or `task_plan/**`, so green CI proves no callability for tools named only there. An existing researched manifest entry at `unused` grants nothing: OPS1 auto-adds vendor-new tools only at that inert value. Promotion to `required` is hand-authored with the calling prose in the SAME commit (manifest EDIT DISCIPLINE); never mechanically promote. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-06.)*

**Concurrency.** `concurrency: group: merge-validated-pr` serializes selected workflow executions; GitHub's strict branch protection and the explicit current-main ancestry guard enforce freshness. GitHub can replace a pending run in the same concurrency group, so never infer landing from dispatch acceptance or wait for a later run to discover a branch. Each routine confirms its OWN PR's merged state and ancestry; if a selected dispatch was cancelled, recheck its PR/head/main/checks before a bounded retry. Concurrent main advances require updating only the assigned branch and fresh checks. Conflicting or timed-out PRs remain open and visible for follow-up, with no broad adoption or automatic branch sweep.

**Cleanup.** The routine itself never deletes branches. The one deletion is done by the Merge validated PR workflow: after a confirmed merge it deletes the selected PR's own head branch, and only while that branch still points at the merged head commit (`.github/scripts/merge_validated_pr.py`; owner direction 2026-10-22, because GitHub's repository auto-delete setting does not fire for merges made with the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN`). Leave every other session's branch intact; any wider cleanup requires separate explicit owner direction. A lingering branch is not itself proof of a failed landing: use the selected PR's merged state and commit ancestry.

## Human role

The human acts on routine output only. The human does effectively one thing:

1. **Confirms crafted orders.** Claude crafts the exact order via the IBKR connector (`create_order_instruction`) and surfaces a tap-to-confirm deep link in chat. `create_order_instruction` itself triggers IBKR's own order-created notification to the human, so for a craftable order — Equity/ETF, single-leg Options, or an OPT–OPT combo/spread (self-improvement audit ITEM 13, 2026-07-11) — no calendar event is created (2026-07-09 — redundant with the IBKR notification, and the human confirms immediately regardless). The human opens the link, reviews the pre-filled order in IBKR, and confirms it. The human never types ticker, side, quantity, price, type, or duration. (For a structure the connector genuinely cannot craft — mixed-type or FOP/FUT combos, or a `get_combo_identifier` rejection — Claude emits a manual-entry text order block, explicitly labeled, **carried in a `[Claude] Confirm order` calendar event** in place of the deep link — never chat-only, since routine chat is unmonitored and there is no `create_order_instruction` call to trigger an IBKR notification for this case.)

All analytical work — thesis construction, position reviews, research-deferral checkpoints, re-screens, foundation-change assessments, router reviews — runs **autonomously**: in-session in the triggering routine, or via the autonomous analysis queue (`state.open_queue` / `events.queue_events`, queue `PENDING_ANALYSIS`) drained daily by D2. The human is never asked to paste an analysis prompt into a fresh chat; that round-trip is retired.

Three prior actions are **obsolete**: (a) *screenshot capture* — Claude reads positions, balances, live orders, executed fills, and market data directly through the IBKR connector, so no screenshot is ever requested; (b) *persisting Claude-produced files* — Claude writes files directly; (c) *pasting analysis prompts into fresh chats* — analysis runs in-session or via the autonomous analysis queue (`state.open_queue` / `events.queue_events`, queue `PENDING_ANALYSIS`). Claude does not present file contents in chat as fenced code blocks; chat output is reserved for crafted orders and brief acknowledgments.

The human does NOT perform any analytical or monitoring task. If the framework needs analysis, monitoring, parsing, watching, verification, or calculation, Claude does it — either inline in the current routine or via the autonomous analysis queue (`events.queue_events`, queue `PENDING_ANALYSIS`) drained daily by D2. Examples of work the human does NOT perform: verifying commissions; making EV decisions; monitoring markets intraday; parsing earnings prints; deciding execute-vs-skip on staged orders; deciding override-vs-honor on NO-GO recommendations; choosing convergence targets, position sizes, limit prices, or invalidation criteria.

If a workflow would require the human to do anything beyond confirming crafted orders, that workflow is broken and Claude must redesign it before staging anything.

**Routine chat is unmonitored — deliver orders through IBKR or the calendar.** For every craftable order (Equity/ETF, single-leg Options, OPT–OPT combo/spread), call `create_order_instruction` to craft and send IBKR's notification for immediate confirmation; create no `[Claude] Confirm order` event. For a genuinely non-craftable structure (mixed-type/FOP combo or a `get_combo_identifier` rejection), put the explicitly labelled manual-entry block in a `[Claude] Confirm order` calendar event with an event-time notification. Self-check that every staged order has its corresponding delivery; chat alone reaches nobody.

## Decision discipline

Claude resolves every decision the framework requires — execute or skip, GO or NO-GO, target selection, sizing, timing, invalidation criteria, marginal-conviction-but-criteria-cleared cases — without human input.

A decision is resolved by the framework's criteria. Any setup that mechanically clears all entry criteria stages automatically, regardless of conviction level. Strategy.md criterion 4 already requires "no decisive flaw," not "high conviction"; conviction is an internal calibration metric persisted to `events.decision_log` but is not a separate gate. The HCA precedent (~45–50% conviction, all criteria cleared, staged) is the canonical handling: if criteria clear, stage with conviction noted; if a criterion fails, decline. There is no middle category requiring human adjudication.

If a decision genuinely cannot be made without information Claude does not have, Claude defers to a future routine or calendar-triggered session where the missing information will be available. Deferral constraints:

- Each deferral names its resolving trigger (specific date/information source) and trigger-failure default.
- Default always takes the conservative branch (skip trade, decline GO, exit position), never another deferral.
- Deferrals do not chain: session 2 resolves session 1's deferral or takes its default; no session-3 re-deferral.
- **ONE EXCEPTION — a single date correction for an ESTIMATED trigger date (owner decision 2026-10-27, interactive triage of W5's `spec_defect_notice_stalled` `9d17f578` on D2's notice `18834121`).** Enqueuer marks estimated external-event dates `due_date_basis: estimate`, issuer/authority-published dates `due_date_basis: issuer`. If the drain finds the event NOT YET OCCURRED and a newly issuer/authority-published future date, it may correct an `estimate` item's `due_date` ONCE to that date, NEVER another estimate; corrected row carries `date_corrected: true` and any further miss takes its conservative default.

## Commission policy

Commissions are NOT factored into staging-time GO/NO-GO decisions, target selection, sizing, or EV computation. Commissions are accepted as a fixed business cost. Implications:

- Thesis construction does not produce "EV at design size" calculations net of commissions.
- `events.decision_log` entries do not document "negative-EV-at-design-size acknowledgment" sections.
- Staged orders are not annotated with EV-at-order-ticket caveats.
- The strategy-level edge-decay metrics (EV per trade in Strategy C and D pre-mortems) continue to function as designed; they measure realized P&L which already nets commissions out empirically.
- Commission paid is captured per-trade in `events.trade_fills` at fill (D2 Step 0 reconciliation), for after-the-fact accounting and 30-trade-gate calibration. It does not enter pre-trade decisions.

## Calendar MCP usage

**Policy (revised 2026-07-09 — supersedes "the calendar is the binding surface for every order/every hard-stop" below).** Two channels already exist that are faster and no less reliable than a calendar event, and duplicating them was pure overhead: (1) `create_order_instruction` itself fires IBKR's own order-created notification the moment a craftable order is staged, and (2) `ops.sp_raise_alert(...)` is picked up by `ops/monitoring/alert_emailer.gs`'s 2-hourly poll of `ops.alerts` and emailed automatically. Both are already-mandatory steps in the staging/failure-alert flows below — so a calendar event on top is redundant for the ordinary case, and the operator confirmed they act on the IBKR/email notification immediately regardless. The calendar is now created in exactly two cases, where nothing else reaches the human:

1. **Non-craftable order (manual-entry fallback).** The IBKR connector genuinely cannot craft the order — a mixed-type or FOP/FUT combo, or a structure `get_combo_identifier` rejects (self-improvement audit ITEM 13, 2026-07-11 — single-leg Options and OPT–OPT combos/spreads, including Strategy C's defined-risk structures, ARE connector-craftable; this fallback is no longer the default path for options). No `create_order_instruction` call means no IBKR notification either, so the manual-entry text order block is carried in a `[Claude] Confirm order` event — the only place it reaches the human.
2. **BigQuery unreachable at connector pre-flight.** `ops.alerts` lives in BigQuery, so if BigQuery itself is down, `sp_raise_alert` can't run and `alert_emailer.gs` has nothing to poll — a `[Claude] ATTENTION — RE-AUTH BigQuery connector` event is the only surviving channel (see Observability below).

Every other staged order (craftable Equity/ETF — the normal case) and every other hard-stop/anomaly (IBKR unreachable once BigQuery is confirmed live, cash tripwire, connector-sanity halt, freshness-gate failure, `missed_confirmation`, etc.) relies on the IBKR notification / `ops.sp_raise_alert` + `alert_emailer.gs` email alone — **no calendar event.** Claude-only analysis was already never placed on the calendar: routine chat is unmonitored and these steps need no human, so they run in-session in the triggering routine or via the autonomous analysis queue (`events.queue_events`, queue `PENDING_ANALYSIS`; next subsection). Recurring cadence work (D1, D2, …, A3) runs as routines and is not on the calendar.

Conventions for the `[Claude] Confirm order` events Claude creates (case 1 above only):

- **Title:** `[Claude] Confirm order — <ticker> <BUY/SELL>`.
- **Time:** **07:00 MT pre-market on the order day**, 30 min before the 07:30 MT open; never adjust for human availability/load.
- **Throughput:** no slot cap; never stagger/defer to spread load.
- **Description:** summary `SIDE QTY TICKER TYPE LIMIT TIF`, explicitly labeled manual-entry order block (no `url`, since uncraftable), and "Enter this order manually in IBKR, confirm at or after market open."
- **Time zone / "today":** query authoritative `state.trading_day_today` (`bigquery/09_market_calendar.sql`) for `today` / `is_trading_day` / `last_trading_day` / `next_trading_day` (America/Denver; `events.market_holidays`, W5/FMP auto-extends). Dated calendar create/delete/filter and queue `due_date` use `.today`, NEVER assistant `currentDate` or Bash `date`. **NARROW EXCEPTION — an `ORDER_STAGED` row's `due_date` (`entry_window_close`) is NOT `.today` (added 2026-09-10, after this bullet was traced as the instruction that produced the defect).** All orders are `DAY` (Operating_Protocols.md §11): `entry_window_close` must be **>= session S actually reached**, `.today` intraday, `.next_trading_day` post-close; if intent expires before S, do not craft, set terminal and log. `state.staged_order_window_invalid` (`bigquery/233_staged_order_window_dead_on_arrival.sql`) / `ops.sp_sq_daily_staging_cap_check` surface `staged_order_window_dead_on_arrival`. Exception ONLY for `queue='ORDER_STAGED'`; all other lanes (`PENDING_ANALYSIS`, `PENDING_DRAFT`, `PENDING_REGIME_REFRESH`, …) retain `.today`, and W4 §C HARD CHECK forbids a next-day default. Do not generalize between an order deadline and tonight's analysis. Binds D2/D2a/D3/W4/M4/Q4/A1/A3.
- **Notification:** alarm at event-time; human enters/confirms. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-07.)*

Conventions for the `[Claude] ATTENTION — RE-AUTH BigQuery connector` event (case 2 above): see the connector pre-flight step, Observability below.

`Confirm order` (manual-entry only) and `ATTENTION — RE-AUTH BigQuery connector` are now the only two canonical calendar event types. Everything formerly scheduled as a `[Claude]` analysis event — thesis construction, scheduled re-screens, research-deferral checkpoints, foundation-change assessments, constraint-relaxation reviews, router reviews — is done in-session or queued (next subsection); and every craftable-order confirmation / ordinary hard-stop alert now relies on IBKR's notification / `alert_emailer.gs` instead of the calendar.

## Observability — run logging & failure alerts

Cross-cutting observability calls (`bigquery/10_observability.sql`, `bigquery/12_cadence_monitor.sql`) **bind ALL routines declared in `ops/cadence.yaml`, including future additions**: D1–D3, D2a, OPS0–OPS2, W1–W5, M1a–M5, M1R, Q1–Q4, A1–A3, SL1–SL5 and AR_att/AR_orc. D2's RUN LOGGING and §13 cash-tripwire alert are worked examples; make the shared calls without duplicating per-routine blocks.

- **Connector pre-flight (FIRST — before run-logging, the dependency gate, or any routine's own Step 0).** Prove each required connector with one trivial read: **BigQuery** every routine, `SELECT * FROM `stock-trading-498512.state.trading_day_today`` (also supplies `today`); **IBKR** D1/D2, `get_account_summary`; **Calendar** 1-day `list_events` for staging routines D2/D3/M4/Q4/A1/A3/AR_orc (non-craftable orders only; Calendar MCP usage). D1/W4 stage nothing and are exempt; W4 BOUNDARY forbids Calendar—restore this probe AND lift that prohibition if W4 gains staging. Apply TRANSIENT-FAILURE WAIT-AND-RETRY before failure disposition; only non-waitable/exhausted errors reach these branches.
  - **BigQuery unreachable (token expired / re-auth required).** Alert sink is down: no `sp_raise_alert`/`ops.alerts` write. Immediately create **`[Claude] ATTENTION — RE-AUTH BigQuery connector`** calendar event unless one exists this incident. **D1** proceeds DEGRADED (IBKR book/marks, prior Daily.md regime, defer ALL BigQuery side-writes, exact 2026-06-26 Daily.md banner). **D2/D2a/D3** HALT, no missing/stale-state work or orders: D2a unconditional reconciliation and D2's six NOT-BLOCKED items override only TRADING-ENABLE, never connector-down; obey own CONNECTOR-DOWN limb, and D2 must not edit Watchlist.md. AR_att HALTS, never emits "No adversarial reviews due for attacker today." Other routines follow FLEET CONNECTOR-DOWN DISPOSITION TABLE. Escalate the existing event in place per INCIDENT INHERITANCE, never create a second; inspect description BEFORE amending (8,192-character cap; replacement updates). If it ends mid-sentence, leave it intact and put this slot's account in its repo record, never rewrite ~8 KB to join a thread. Keep a short stable ACTION-REQUIRED banner pointing to ONE per-incident repo file slots append to (table items (1)/(2)); freshness/cadence dead-man switches record the miss on recovery, RUNBOOK §26 resolves. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-08.)*

    - **FLEET CONNECTOR-DOWN DISPOSITION TABLE.** A routine's own CONNECTOR-DOWN DISPOSITION limb (D2a, D2, AR_att, SL2) or AR_orc's UPSTREAM-HALT LIMB governs; this table is the default and must be corrected if it disagrees. A cadence routine absent from the table defaults to HALT with the uniform owes below. `ops/cadence.yaml` governs `catchup_safe` and queue-driven membership. Both catch-up paths use `state.catchup_refire_readiness`: primary OPS2 inline execution, fallback OPS0 STEP 2 re-fire and `catchup_refire_blocked` email.

      | Routine | Disposition | Own limb | After re-auth |
      |---|---|---|---|
      | D1 | DEGRADED (rule above) | — | `catchup_safe`; a degraded run writes no `ops.run_log` row, so the slot still reads as missed and the catch-up path replays it |
      | D2a, D2 | HALT | CONNECTOR-DOWN DISPOSITION (each) | not `catchup_safe`, never-refire set: no automatic replay; OPS0 STEP 2b raises the manual-rerun notice; the next regular fire otherwise |
      | AR_att, SL2 | HALT | CONNECTOR-DOWN DISPOSITION (each) | queue-driven, not `catchup_safe`: no replay owed; the next regular fire picks up (due predicates are `<= today`) |
      | AR_orc | HALT | UPSTREAM-HALT LIMB (AR_att's limb cascades to it) | as AR_att |
      | SL5 | HALT | — | as AR_att |
      | M1R | HALT | — | queue-driven AND `catchup_safe`: replayed by the catch-up path; its due predicate is `<= today` |
      | D3, OPS1, SL3, W1, W2, W3, W4, W5, M1a, M1b, M2, M3, M5, Q1, Q2, Q3, SL1, A1, A2 | HALT | — | `catchup_safe`: the missed slot is replayed by the catch-up path |
      | M4, SL4, Q4, A3 | HALT | — | not `catchup_safe`, never-refire set: OPS0 STEP 2b manual-rerun notice; the next regular fire otherwise |
      | OPS0, OPS2 | HALT | — | not `catchup_safe`: no replay owed; the next regular fire |

    - **WHAT EVERY HALTED SLOT OWES (uniform; D1 in DEGRADED MODE owes (1) only and keeps its own deferred-writes record).**
      1. **Calendar.** Only if absent, create `[Claude] ATTENTION — RE-AUTH BigQuery connector`: short stable ACTION-REQUIRED banner, claude.ai connector re-authorization→RUNBOOK §26, incident repo path. Later slots add ≤1 `UPDATE hh:mm MDT <slot> halted`, cap-check first; never rewrite thread.
      2. **Per-incident repo record.** First detector creates `ops/spikes/bigquery-deauth-<operating-date>-<slot>-halt-record.md` (America/Denver); later slots APPEND `## <slot> slot, <date>: HALTED` to SAME file. RUNBOOK §48 subject, no routine-id prefix.
      3. **No `ops.run_log` backfill after re-auth**; dead-man switches record misses.
      4. **Never emit a "nothing due" / quiet-day line**; state/queue are UNKNOWN.
      5. **Findings.** Unreachable `ops.alerts` means never claim "filed"; one owner/surface bullet per finding under `## Unfiled findings` (RUNBOOK §26 step 4; OPS0 intake).
      6. **The record's RECOVERY PROCEDURE names EVERY declared dependent of the halted routine (added 2026-10-11, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing SL3's `halt_record_replay_order_omits_catchup_safe_downstream`, alert `da0310fb-c7cd-46cb-bb55-4943089fb9b4`).** Replay-order AND expected-signature lists include EVERY `ops/cadence.yaml depends_on` consumer, even `catchup_safe` needing no replay; say: "own catch-up loop; recovers once the upstream's catch-up lands".
  - **IBKR unreachable (BigQuery up).** `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('critical', '<ID>', 'connector', 'IBKR connector unreachable at pre-flight', '<JSON>')`, log `'halted'` and ABORT (D1/D2 require this pre-flight); BigQuery/alert_emailer delivers, no calendar event.
  - **Calendar unreachable (BigQuery up; staging routines only).** `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning', '<ID>', 'connector', 'Calendar connector unreachable at pre-flight — craftable orders unaffected, non-craftable orders cannot be surfaced this session', '<JSON>')` and proceed with craftable orders (IBKR notifies). Hard-stop (`CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('critical', ...)`, `'halted'`, ABORT) ONLY when actually about to stage a non-craftable order whose manual-entry block cannot be surfaced another way. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-09.)*

  This makes a connector de-auth a seconds-to-detect, single-channel-surfaced event for **every** routine rather than a mid-run partial failure — the RUNBOOK §26 blast-radius mitigation. (D1 already did exactly this ad-hoc on 2026-06-26; this makes it uniform and first.)

- **TRANSIENT-FAILURE WAIT-AND-RETRY (owner directive 2026-07-18) — binds ALL routines; applies to EVERY external call in the run** (pre-flight, BigQuery query/DML, IBKR/Calendar/GitHub/web-fetch), BEFORE degrade/halt/alert routing. Wait in-session for errors time alone can plausibly fix, unless the wait would outlive the session.
  - **DIAGNOSE BY PROBE, ONCE PER INCIDENT (v2, 2026-07-18 adversarial review):** On the first unexpected BigQuery-side failure, ONE `SELECT 1`, then failing-statement dry-run ONLY if ambiguous; classify behavior: `SELECT 1` fails: auth wording → RE-AUTH, otherwise waitable connector/service outage. Pass + fresh-scan "Custom quota exceeded"/`QueryUsagePerUserPerDay` → non-waitable **DAILY-QUOTA SIGNATURE**; metadata/dry-run/cached/0-byte success cannot exclude it, check per-user override (RUNBOOK §2). Pass + deterministic `invalid`/`notFound` → code/schema, non-waitable; intermittent → ladder. Never repeat incident probes at later rungs.
  - **WAITABLE — retry in-session:** rate/short-window/concurrency quota limits (`rateLimitExceeded`/`jobRateLimitExceeded`/concurrent-or-per-minute `quotaExceeded`, 429/503), `backendError`/`internalError`/5xx/timeouts/dropped connections, MCP errors/hangs without auth/permission wording (including IBKR gateway), git push/fetch network failure, read-after-write lag (retry READ, never blindly rewrite).
  - **NON-WAITABLE — route immediately per the existing branches, do NOT retry:** auth/permission (`accessDenied`/401/403/token-expired), SQL syntax/schema (`invalid`/`notFound`), trading-enable/order-guard aborts, data-integrity failure (cash tripwire/dual-path disagreement), daily-window quotas. Unsatisfied `sp_assert_deps` uses its SEPARATE DEPENDENCY-WAIT WINDOW (~10-min polls/~60-min base), never this ladder. `QueryUsagePerUserPerDay` resets midnight US/Pacific; exhaustion violates RUNBOOK §2's NON-binding-cap policy: raise LATCHING `bigquery_quota_exhausted`, halt/degrade per pre-flight, retry next scheduled fire/OPS0. Only human or INCIDENT INHERITANCE verified-clear resolves it, never mechanical resolver.
  - **MCP-TRANSPORT REJECTION — THE ONE CARVE-OUT FROM "NON-WAITABLE", AND IT GETS A ZERO-WAIT RETRY (2026-09-11, closing the fleet-wide `mcp_arg_drop_rate` reports).** **`Required parameter is missing: query`** despite supplied query, or another argument-shaped MCP-layer error, with NO provider job (no `queryId`, no billed bytes, no matching job in `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT`) → ONE immediate IDENTICAL re-issue before ladder; WRITE SAFETY applies. Never shorten/rewrite/simplify. If recovered, use `RETRY[kind=mcp_arg_drop;n=1;waited_s=0;outcome=recovered]`, proceed, no alert/degrade/halt. Real SQL-level `invalid`/`notFound` or `queryId` remains non-waitable.
  - **IF THE IMMEDIATE RE-ISSUE ALSO FAILS, RETRY IT AGAIN — DO NOT INFER A SIZE LIMIT (corrected 2026-09-11; an earlier cut of this bullet asserted a ~13KB request ceiling and that was WRONG).** **THERE IS NO DEMONSTRATED REQUEST-SIZE CEILING.** Repeat identically; persistent failure → run-issue connector incident with verbatim error/request size, artifact INTACT, never size diagnosis.
  - **SYNCHRONOUS-TIMEOUT HANDOFF — NOT A FAILURE AT ALL, AND RE-ISSUING IT IS THE ONE THING THAT CORRUPTS DATA (2026-09-13).** `execute_sql`/`execute_sql_readonly` **`{"jobComplete": false, "jobId": "job_..."}`** means accepted RUNNING: poll exact `jobId` with `get_query_results` to `jobComplete: true`, then read rows. NEVER re-issue/use ladder: SELECT double-bills; INSERT/UPDATE/MERGE/DELETE/CALL double-writes. Do not conflate MCP-transport NO-job rejection. Lost id → WRITE SAFETY effect-read before re-run (RUNBOOK §52).
  - **THE LADDER (bounded, same session):** attempt → ~60 s wait → retry → ~5 min wait → retry → ~10 min wait → final retry (4 attempts/~16 min; no immediate retry except MCP). Apply ±20% jitter; honor an explicit server `Retry-After`/`retryDelay` instead, capped at 10 min. Bash `sleep <seconds>` needs covering `timeout`, ≤600 s/call (chain if needed). Cumulative waits ≤30 min/session; further/exceeding-cap waits non-waitable. **Never wait past 23:30 America/Denver**, also the dependency-window clamp.
  - **WRITE SAFETY:** Before repeating failed DML/insert/order calls, verify effect absent (row query; IBKR `get_account_orders`); uncertain → effect-READ. `create_order_instruction`: one retry ONLY after no-order confirmation (staging atomicity), NEVER blind.
  - **INCIDENT INHERITANCE (v2, 2026-07-18) — one incident, one alert thread.** M1a/M1R apply this and verified-clear METADATA-ONLY for `category = 'bigquery_quota_exhausted'`; non-blind routines handle `connector`. Waitable failure + readable `ops.alerts`: FIRST match unresolved same symptom, ANY age for LATCHING (default outside `ops.alert_policy` non-latching allowlist; includes `connector`/`bigquery_quota_exhausted`), last 24 h otherwise. Match → ONE probe instead of ladder, `{"related_alert_id":"<id>"}` in any raised payload, `INCIDENT[ref=<alert_id>]` in note; new alert ONLY for MATERIAL severity/blast-radius change. Never downgrade genuinely new incidents below `warning`. **Verified-clear:** successful pre-flight FRESH table scan → clear earlier `bigquery_quota_exhausted`/BigQuery-referencing `connector`: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note='verified clear: fresh table scan succeeded, <ID> pre-flight <ts>' WHERE alert_id='<id>' AND resolved=FALSE`. Only those two BigQuery-infra classes; capital-affecting classes remain human-only, and a BigQuery probe never clears IBKR/Calendar connector alerts.
  - **OUTCOME LOGGING:** Recovered → normal status, terminal narrative `transient <kind> x<n>, waited ~<m>m, recovered`, ONE exact `RETRY[kind=<slug>;n=<attempts>;waited_s=<total>;outcome=recovered|exhausted]` per incident (including closing bracket; `state.retry_telemetry`, bigquery/88). Exhausted → existing Failure-alerts failed/halted, exhaustion in alert and `error_msg`/`<note>`.
  - Narrower Session-end push backoff, AR_orc echo-suspect cool-off, order-guard next-run re-evaluation and D3 no-retry trigger-create retain precedence. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-10.)*

- **Alert auto-resolve (every run, right after connector pre-flight) — BEST-EFFORT, never gates.** `CALL ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()` (`bigquery/34_alert_lifecycle.sql`, self-improvement audit WP2, 2026-07-07), wrapped so a failure here can never abort the routine:

BEGIN
CALL stock-trading-498512.ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts();
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN SELECT @@error.message; -- swallow: cleanup must not abort the routine
END;

Auto-resolve re-checks the `ops.alert_policy` non-latching allowlist (`missing_dependency`, `missed_run`, `routine_stalled`, `catchup_refire_blocked`, `staleness` echo); Rule 5 closes delivered roster warnings and Rule 6 closes recovered `scheduled_query_stale` warnings. `trading_halted` is no longer human-only: Rule 7 closes it only while its policy is `latching=FALSE`, each of `state.trading_enabled` and `state.trading_enabled_mechanical` returns exactly one row with `trading_enabled=TRUE` and `halt_reason` NULL, and no unresolved critical `missing_dependency` exists. `cash_tripwire`/`order_guard_block` remain human-only, drilled monthly by `ops.sp_fire_drill_alert_latch`; other categories follow their registered resolve rules. Run it before trading-enable reads and the dependency gate to clear healed transients. Both `ops.sp_assert_trading_enabled` and `ops.sp_assert_trading_enabled_mechanical` also call `sp_auto_resolve_alerts()` first, best-effort, so just-healed alerts clear even after an earlier preamble call. *(History: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-11.)*

- **PRE-REFRESH HALT DISPOSITION — a gate that is FALSE only because today's marks are not in yet is NOT an incident (added 2026-09-01, `ops.alerts` `a5bb4024-887a-4ead-919f-6120088808cc`; `bigquery/206_staging_halt_prerefresh_disposition.sql`).** `.last_trading_day` becomes today at Denver midnight before D2a writes marks/perf, so pre-refresh `state.freshness.marks_fresh`/`engine_fresh` and `state.trading_enabled` FALSE are normal. D2a is OUT OF SCOPE: `state.trading_enabled_mechanical` lacks those freshness terms (`bigquery/176`). Q4/A3 craft no orders, so `defer_to_craft_site` raises nothing. `trading_halted` is non-latching (`ops.alert_policy latching=FALSE`); `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts` Rule 7 closes it only when each gate view returns exactly one row with `trading_enabled=TRUE`, `halt_reason` NULL and no critical `missing_dependency` open, without changing gates. Never hand-close a row the resolver owns: `CALL ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()`. Keep the `defer_to_craft_site` branch; **at a TRADING-ENABLE GATE read choose the alert by `state.staging_halt_disposition.gate_alert_action`**, as follows: *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-12.)*

```
SELECT trading_enabled, halt_reason, gate_alert_action, disposition_note
FROM `stock-trading-498512.state.staging_halt_disposition`;
```

  - `raise_critical` (or the view is unreadable, or the column is NULL) — raise the `trading_halted` critical exactly as this routine's gate step spells it out. **This is the default; anything unexpected lands here.**
  - `defer_to_craft_site` — raise NOTHING at the gate. Carry the FALSE verdict forward unchanged and record `disposition_note` in the `sp_routine_end` `<note>`. If this routine later DECLINES AN ACTUAL ORDER CRAFT because of that verdict, raise the critical THEN, at that craft site, with `<halt_reason>` in the payload — that is the moment real work is lost, and it is the only moment worth an operator email. A routine that crafts no orders on this run raises nothing at all.

  **THE GATE VERDICT IS UNAFFECTED.** `gate_alert_action` selects severity only: `defer_to_craft_site` leaves `trading_enabled` FALSE and every craft point blocked. `halt_is_prerefresh_artifact` requires schedule-derived `marks_current` AND `engine_current` (`bigquery/173`); a D2a failure makes them FALSE and restores `raise_critical` within ~6h. Every NULL fails closed to `raise_critical`.

- **EMBEDDING-LAG REPAIR BEFORE ANY TRADING-ENABLE READ (added 2026-08-17, AR_orc) — BEST-EFFORT, never gates; ONE statement, not a retry ladder.** Before any `state.trading_enabled` / `state.trading_enabled_mechanical` / `state.b3_trading_enabled_check` read, best-effort `CALL ops.sp_embed_pending()` (Alert auto-resolve wrapper), then read the gate ONCE as authoritative.
  - TRANSIENT-FAILURE NON-WAITABLE forbids a second read/wait/backoff to wait out a control gate; D2's own once-only `sp_auto_resolve_alerts()` re-read is unchanged.
  - `bigquery/176_decouple_embedding_health_from_trading_gate.sql` removed embedding from all three gates: it affects `state.system_health.embeddings_healthy` and `find_precedents`, while `ops.sp_sq_daily_freshness_check`'s critical `staleness` is excluded from `blocking_criticals` (`category NOT IN ('trading_halted', 'staleness')`). Keep repair best-effort for searchability; never claim embedding gates trading or hard-stop on it (Failure alerts).
  - **DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE** is superseded by `bigquery/176`; never re-propose the closed gate-ordering finding. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-13.)*

- **ROSTER-CHANGE NOTICES (owner directive 2026-08-04) — the six SISA transitions that MUST reach the operator's inbox.** Autonomous add/delete requires no approval; notify every membership change. These six categories — `strategy_shadow_registered`, `strategy_probe_registered`, `strategy_graduated`, `retirement_proposed`, `strategy_deregistered`, `roster_below_floor` — are raised at **`warning`**, NEVER `info` (filtered by email/relay) or `critical` (halts staging). All are non-latching, auto-resolved once `notified_ts IS NOT NULL` (Rule 5, `bigquery/134_roster_change_notifications.sql`); no human UPDATE. **EMAIL ONLY**, deliberately no ntfy (`scripts/alert_relay.py` NO_PUSH_CATEGORIES/query; owner 2026-09-07). Keep this set identical here, `alert_emailer.gs` ROSTER_NOTICE_CATEGORIES, Rule 5 IN list, and relay NO_PUSH_CATEGORIES; blocking `scripts/check_roster_notice_lockstep.py` checks all four. Add to all four or none. **Payload contract:** exact renderer keys `strategy_code`, `strategy_name`, `from_state`, `to_state`, `roster_active_before`, `roster_active_after`, `capital_usd` (risk dollars in/out;0 if none), `pct_nav`, `reason` (one-line thesis/decay/kill trigger), `git_commit`, `lifecycle_event_id`; retirement/termination also `kill_trigger`. Renderer tolerates missing/malformed payload, so `<message>` MUST independently be a complete sentence naming strategy/transition. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-14.)*

- **Run logging (every run) — BEST-EFFORT, copy the template.** Logging must never break work; wrap EACH CALL best-effort and copy argument lists verbatim. START:
  ```
  BEGIN
    CALL `stock-trading-498512.ops.sp_routine_start`('<ID>', <today (America/Denver, from state.trading_day_today)>,
      <session_id>, <branch>, '<the VERBATIM trigger instruction this session received>');
  EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN SELECT @@error.message;  -- swallow: logging must not abort the routine
  END;
  ```
  **THE START ROW MUST COME FROM `sp_routine_start` WITH A NON-NULL INSTRUCTION — NEVER FROM A DIRECT `sp_log_run('…','started',…)` CALL (added 2026-10-04, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing AR_orc's `run_log_started_row_missing_instruction`, alert `82211222-7c00-43bc-a784-f4a0e53e256c`).** Wrapper populates `ops.run_log.instruction`, feeding `state.routine_last_instruction`/`state.instruction_drift`; repair own NULL-instruction start by UPDATE scoped to own `run_id` (sp_amend_run_note precedent). Deferred fleet detector (view/cadence raise/policy/SQ_VERSION) stays unbuilt unless fresh incidence rises outside SL slots.
  END in the same wrapper: `'completed'`, or aborted `'failed'`/`'halted'` with specific diagnostic `error_msg`. `ops.sp_log_run` uses `error_msg` (then `<note>`, then literal fallback) for `routine_run_failed` and completed-with-error `routine_run_warning` inbox detail (`bigquery/230_run_outcome_notification.sql`); never supply placeholders/blank diagnostic when there is an issue. **Gate `'completed'` on a verified remote push** AND confirmed own-PR main landing (§Session end), otherwise failed/halted:
  ```
  BEGIN
    CALL `stock-trading-498512.ops.sp_routine_end`('<ID>', <today>, 'completed', <session_id>, <branch>, <rows_written>, NULL, <note>);
  EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN SELECT @@error.message;
  END;
  ```
  `<instruction>` is the VERBATIM scheduled trigger, even an ad-hoc session reusing a routine id (e.g. `Read Claude_Task_Plan.md. Perform D2 — regular routine.`); put one-off work in `<note>`/`session_id`, never instruction. Canonical `ops.run_log.instruction` → `state.routine_last_instruction` verifies live drift against `scripts/print_routines.py` (RUNBOOK §22); freeform notes are ignored. Missing completion arms freshness/cadence dead-man switches (`state.freshness`, `state.cadence_watch`/`cadence_check.sql`) and audit trail; table-based marks_fresh/engine_fresh independently gate all_green. A routine auto-monitors after a completed run in the last 14 days. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-15.)*

  **`<rows_written>` COUNTS BIGQUERY ROWS THIS RUN INSERTED — NOTHING ELSE (pinned 2026-08-07).** Not repo files edited, not tickers touched, not decisions made. The definition had never been written down, and on 2026-08-07 D2 logged `rows_written=5` for a run that inserted exactly ONE BigQuery row — the other four were `Watchlist.md` ticker edits counted as though they were rows. Nothing broke (the field is read by no gate, view or dead-man's switch), but `ops.run_log` is the first thing every audit and incident reconstruction reads, and a field that means different things in different runs is worse than an absent one. Count the rows you actually `INSERT`/`CALL`-insert, break the total down in `<note>`, and make the breakdown add up to the number you pass. Repo output belongs in `<note>` and in the commit, never in this integer.

  **EXCLUDE THE RUN'S OWN `ops.run_log` ROWS.** Its `sp_routine_start`/`sp_routine_end` inserts are logging rather than output; excluding them keeps `rows_written` comparable across runs.

  **`<note>` IS MANDATORY ON EVERY TERMINAL ROW.** `completed`/`failed`/`halted` need real narrative of decisions, measurements and deliberate non-actions, including no-ops. `state.run_log_content_gaps`/`ops.sp_sq_cadence_check` `run_log_note_missing` detects NULL/blank terminal notes (`bigquery/147_run_log_content_quality.sql`), deliberately not terminal instruction (belongs on start). **NEVER SHORTEN A NOTE TO MAKE A FAILING WRITE SUCCEED (2026-09-11).** `Required parameter is missing: query` from `sp_routine_end`/`sp_amend_run_note`/`sp_log_decision`/`sp_write_adversarial_review` is MCP-TRANSPORT REJECTION: re-issue IDENTICALLY once, then again if needed per TRANSIENT-FAILURE; never infer note size or trim (no demonstrated request-size ceiling). Pre-digest transcript shortening passes SHA-256 checks, so checksum cannot protect against this corruption. `ops.sp_amend_run_note` (`bigquery/170_run_log_note_write_time_guard.sql`) fills ONLY blank terminal notes from an in-progress run, no older than 6 h; it rejects nonblank/nonterminal/older rows (`REFUSED: no eligible row … it does not rewrite history`). No append/extend/history rewrite or workaround here: late detail belongs in `events.decision_log` or next run's note. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-16.)*

  **THE `ops.web_calls` BATCH INSERT BELONGS HERE — immediately before the terminal call above (pinned 2026-08-19).** Metered external calls part(d) requires ONE `ops.web_calls` row per Tavily/`web_search`/`web_fetch`/FMP/HF call, batched in ONE INSERT inside this best-effort finishing wrapper (`bigquery/174_web_call_telemetry.sql`). Missing rows alone cannot distinguish zero calls from omitted telemetry; when `state.web_spend_month.has_unreported_runs` TRUE, W5 EXTERNAL-SPEND DIGEST names those routines and reports spend as FLOOR, never total (State provenance). **SO AFFIRM A ZERO IN `<note>` — ONE BLANKET LINE, NOT A PER-SURFACE DENIAL (added 2026-08-30, closes the `telemetry_zero_affirmation_scope` info alert).** Every no-row run must use one blanket line covering orchestrator/ALL sub-agents and ALL metered surfaces: `METERED SPEND: ZERO. No Tavily, web_search, web_fetch, FMP or HF call by the orchestrator or ANY sub-agent — every fact came from BigQuery, the IBKR connector, or repo files, all free. Consequently no ops.web_calls rows are owed or written — an honest zero, not an omission.` Missing/ambiguous affirmation raises `web_call_coverage_gap`; its row-bearing resolve path cannot clear a quiet run. Binds EVERY `expected_metered` routine, including conditional callers: D1/D2a/W1/W2/W3/W5/M1a/M2/M3/Q2/Q3/SL1/OPS1/OPS2 (`bigquery/200_web_call_coverage_obligation_floor.sql`). *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-17.)*

- **CATCH-UP EVIDENCE WINDOW (owner directive 2026-07-25) — every routine, right after run logging, BEST-EFFORT, never gates.** Evidence reaches **(own last successful completion, now]**: `SELECT window_start_ts, never_completed, window_days FROM state.routine_catchup_window WHERE routine='<ID>'` (`bigquery/105_routine_catchup_window.sql`); last completed `ops.run_log` timestamp, or cadence-sized `ops/cadence.yaml` monitor-class fallback if `never_completed`. For evidence reads (Daily.md scans, decision-log lookbacks/file diffs), replace "today"/last-run/week/month/quarter lower bounds ONLY when this reaches further back; never narrow them.
  - **WHY (the aging-alert trap).** Rule 2 `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts` (`bigquery/34_alert_lifecycle.sql`) ages `missed_run` out after >1 day with no completion evidence; never infer coverage from its clearance.
  - **DECISION SCOPING (unchanged).** Widen evidence ONLY; decisions/actions remain current-session: no retroactive orders, backdated staging/period writes or missed-period dates.
  - **MULTI-PERIOD OUTPUT RULE.** First-line markers always CURRENT-period; cover missed periods as labeled body subsections, oldest first before current content.
  - **WRITE-ONCE RULE.** Reuse existing finding/period idempotency keys (`events.decision_log`, catchup miss_keys, dedup); never re-emit durably recorded findings, even across multiple periods.
  - **TELEMETRY.** When `window_days` >1.5x normal cadence lookback (daily>1.5, weekly>10.5 days), add exact `CATCHUP[window_days=<N>]` to completion `<note>`; no token near normal/fallback.
  - **NON-GATING + FALLBACK.** Unreadable/missing/error view → own cadence-default lookback, proceed and note fallback; never halt/degrade for this view.
  - **Reference implementations generalized here — cite, don't reinvent per routine:** D1 SCAN WINDOW marker/git/fixed fallback, D3 golden `git log --since`, W5 since-last-run and SL2/SL5/SL1/AR_att/AR_orc queue drains reference this shared mechanism. Run **HISTORY-DEPTH PRECHECK** BEFORE git-sourced windows (including D1 commit timestamp, D3 golden and D2 Daily.md catch-up); UNDEEPENABLE → non-git BigQuery window, note git unavailable. Do not conflate OWN evidence reach with UPSTREAM DEPENDENCY-WAIT or `catchup_safe` scheduling/refire authority; `catchup_safe:false` routines still use this. Time reach never expands source permissions: AR_att/M1a blinding remains binding. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-18.)*

- **Dependency gate (action routines) — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap.** Before start-log call `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('<ID>', <deps>, <today>)`, separate from best-effort logging; omit with no deps (D2 `['D1']`; W4 `['W1','W2','W3']`; M4 `['M1b','M2','M3']`). Missing monitored-upstream completion raises `missing_dependency` AND aborts. Period classes `weekly_sun`/`monthly_ftd`/`quarterly_ftd`/`annual_ftd` accept ANY completion from downstream's current-period start through today (`bigquery/114_period_aware_dependency_gate.sql`); daily/queue/unrecognized ids require exact-day plus midnight grace, fail-safe for unknown ids. Upstreams not yet logging are self-bootstrap satisfied, becoming gated once monitored.

  **§38 evidence-check — MECHANICAL inside the gate (RUNBOOK §38 layer B).** `ops.sp_assert_deps` (`bigquery/12_cadence_monitor.sql`) first calls `ops.sp_backfill_run_log_from_markers()` unconditionally, best-effort: same-day output on `origin/main` with a CI marker but no completion log self-heals before dependency evaluation. No session-level git-log/backfill is needed before retrying.

  Fallback only if `sp_assert_deps` still aborts (including missing not-yet-written marker): `git log origin/main --oneline --since=<today 00:00 America/Denver> -- <X's known output file>` (D1: Daily.md). This TODAY-only fail-closed check is deliberately exempt from **HISTORY-DEPTH PRECHECK**; widening beyond today requires it. **A HALT RECORD IS NEVER THIS EVIDENCE (added 2026-10-11, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing AR_orc's `dependency_gate_misreads_upstream_halt_record`, alert `d8da6e78-f4f3-4549-8389-91d3be3c3551`, half A):** exclude RUNBOOK §48 subjects (no routine prefix) and commits changing only `ops/spikes/*halt-record*`; only a non-halt commit touching X's REAL output qualifies. If a same-day qualifying commit lacks a marker, `INSERT INTO ops.run_log (routine, run_date, status, note) VALUES ('<X>', <today>, 'completed', 'auto-backfilled from git evidence by <this routine>, RUNBOOK §38 layer B')` and proceed; no qualifying commit → genuine dependency abort.

  **DEPENDENCY-WAIT WINDOW (owner directive 2026-07-18; v2 same day, adversarially reviewed) — an unsatisfied dependency is a WAIT driven by EVIDENCE, not an instant halt and not a blind hour.** If `sp_assert_deps` still aborts after marker backfill/midnight grace/git fallback, best-effort `sp_routine_start` NOW, then poll ~10 min: re-`CALL ops.sp_assert_deps(...)` (reruns backfill), ONE cheap upstream-today `ops.run_log` read, own same-day/in-progress guard recheck. If another session completed/is active, output guard line and END immediately.
  - **Gate PASSES** → proceed; immediately best-effort `CALL ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()` clears first-call `missing_dependency` critical.
  - **Upstream `'started'` within the last ~2h, no terminal row → ALIVE:** keep polling, extend beyond 60 to hard 120 min ceiling.
  - **Upstream terminal `'failed'`/`'halted'` today:** REFIRE once if refireable; otherwise FUTILE, exhaust immediately and note terminal state. Same-day origin/main RUNBOOK §48 `ops/spikes/*-halt-record.md` naming that upstream proves the same condition without a run-log row; REFIRE first if eligible, otherwise FUTILE, cite commit, NEVER fabricate completed.
  - **NO upstream row today**, slot `ops/cadence.yaml time_local` passed ≥45 min: ACTIVE REPAIR once if refireable, else plain 60 min window; re-evaluate EVERY poll. Empty upstream intake follows AR_orc UPSTREAM-HALT LIMB.
  - **Budgets and clamps:** once/run for all deps; 60 min base,120 min alive/refired ceiling; separate from transient 30 min budget; never past 23:30 America/Denver. Earlier-routine same-day open `missing_dependency` covering same chain HALVES window to~30 min. Trading-enable/order-guard aborts remain immediate halts. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-19.)*

  **REFIREABLE** requires upstream `ops/cadence.yaml catchup_safe:true`, id in `ops/trigger_ids.json`, is outside OPS0's scope-guardrail exclusion set (D2, D2a, M4, Q4, A3, SL4), and no `ops.catchup_refire_log` for TIER-AWARE miss_key: daily `'<X>|<today>'`; period W/M/Q/A `'<X>|<period_start>'` with period_start READ from `state.cadence_period_watch`, NEVER own run day (`bigquery/59` literal dedup). W4 is queue-only/catchup-safe; AR_att/AR_orc/SL2/SL5 are false. **ACTIVE REPAIR mechanics — mirror OPS0 STEP 2 exactly:** immediately pre-fire RE-CHECK miss_key log AND upstream ANY run-log row today; if either appeared, SKIP. `RemoteTrigger run(<trig_id>)` → `INSERT INTO ops.catchup_refire_log (miss_key, routine, tier, trigger_id, outcome, note) VALUES ('<tier-aware key>', '<X>', '<daily|period>', '<trig_id>', 'refired', 'refired by <ID> dependency-wait (upstream missing past slot)')` → `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('info', '<ID>', 'catchup_refired', ...)`. Permanent tier-aware dedup makes OPS0 skip; upstream completed/in-progress guard covers late originals. Missing id means not-refireable; self-registration stays OPS0-only.

  **On exhaustion** (window spent, clamp hit, or futile): the EXISTING path — log `'halted'`; the gate's alert stands, with `<note>` and the alert text stating the dependency wait was already exhausted (so a human doesn't hand-wait further) plus the token **`DEPWAIT[dep=<X>;polls=<n>;waited_s=<total>;outcome=satisfied|refired_then_satisfied|futile|exhausted;refired=<X|none>]`** (also appended on SUCCESS — `state.retry_telemetry` parses it); the next scheduled firing / OPS0 catch-up remains the cross-session retry. Maintainer guardrail: this rule assumes today's dependency graph — same-tier deps, and daily upstreams that run every calendar day; a future cross-tier or trading-day-conditional dependency must revisit the slot-passed check and miss_key logic before relying on ACTIVE REPAIR.

  **Midnight-crossing grace (RUNBOOK §41).** Independently of landed-but-unlogged repair, `sp_assert_deps` accepts an upstream completed for `<today> MINUS ONE DAY` only before Denver noon of `<today>`, covering delayed evening execution past midnight. This is automatic; a real gap on both days still aborts.

- **SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD, generalized (completeness-critic finding N-4, 2026-07-16) — binds every `catchup_safe: true` routine in `ops/cadence.yaml`, including W4's queue-only research handoff, PLUS D2 and D2a (rescoped 2026-08-09).** Queue-driven AR_att/AR_orc/SL2/SL5/**M1R** exempt; OPS0 refire-log dedup alone cannot suppress late originals. Check FIRST before logging/deps/work. Scoped routines carry a one-line pointer: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='<ID>' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed'`; >=1 → output "`<ID>` already completed today (a prior fire — OPS0 catch-up or the routine's own scheduled trigger — already completed; this is the expected redundant re-invocation, not an error)." and END IMMEDIATELY, subject to waiver. **ONE-TIME OWNER WAIVER (added 2026-10-20, owner directive in an interactive session; `bigquery/260_guard_waivers.sql`) — binds every routine this bullet binds, and every per-routine pointer below inherits it without restating it.** Before guard-ending read `SELECT waiver_id, reason FROM state.guard_waivers_open WHERE routine='<ID>' AND guard='same_day_double_run'`. None→end; row→CONSUME FIRST: `INSERT INTO ops.guard_waivers (waiver_id, routine, guard, run_date, event, actor, note) VALUES ('<waiver_id>', '<ID>', 'same_day_double_run', <today, America/Denver>, 'CONSUMED', '<ID>:<this session id>', 'consumed by <ID> fire <UTC timestamp>')` (six NOT NULL/no-default columns; `event_id`/`event_ts` default). Proceed normally with `sp_routine_start` and EVERY arsenal/dependency/trading gate; note `double-run guard waived by <waiver_id>`. Only interactive owner grants (`actor owner:<session>`), ONE routine/guard/Denver run_date, single-use CONSUMED closes, expires by `state.trading_day_today`; scheduled routines NEVER grant and no other gate is waived. Evening daily cohort uses its noon-threshold cycle-aware variant. Also END for another session's same-routine/today started row within 3 h lacking terminal; >3h orphan does not suppress.
  - **QUIESCENCE REBUTTAL to the 3h in-flight rule (added 2026-08-18, SL3 — closes the evening-slot unrecoverable-day defect).** Direct liveness overrides the 3 h proxy: read `` `stock-trading-498512.region-us`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT `` since predecessor start and attribute routine work by query shape/timing (project includes scheduled/CI/emailer jobs). Newest attributable job >45 min old → predecessor DEAD, PROCEED and mandatory completion token `DEADPRIOR[prior_started=<HH:MM MT>;last_job=<HH:MM MT>;quiet_min=<N>]`. Compare 45 min to INTER-JOB silence, NEVER total runtime; missing pushed branch/`ops.routine_commit_markers` only corroborates, never proves death.
  - **WHY the rebuttal is needed — the proxy is worst exactly where its cost is highest.** Successor's completed row closes orphan started by `(routine,run_date)` for `state.stalled_runs`; `DEADPRIOR[...]` is required recovery evidence.
  - **VISIBILITY — a suppressed run must not be silent.** Before in-flight END, write ONE `events.decision_log` via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(<today>,'ops-note',...)` naming predecessor start `log_ts`, own timestamp and the quiescence figure that did not exceed 45 min. Write NO run-log row (would falsely satisfy cadence/stalled checks), and no new `ops.alerts` category (unregistered defaults latch); use decision log. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-20.)*

- **RUN-LOG GAP INTERPRETATION — a zero-row day is NOT an outage until `state.fleet_blackout_days` says so (added 2026-08-23, W1 `cadence_outage` false positive `f6ff58ee`).** Before any alert, note or decision-log claim that routines failed to run, resolve it against `bigquery/196_cadence_expected_history.sql`. For FLEET-WIDE claims use `SELECT * FROM state.fleet_blackout_days`: no row for a date means no fleet blackout; zero rows means none in the trailing 90 days. For SINGLE-ROUTINE claims use `SELECT * FROM state.cadence_expected_history WHERE routine = '<ID>' AND run_date = <date>`: missing means `expected AND in_service AND rows_logged = 0`. Do not use the fleet view for a single routine: it has no `routine` column and requires the entire expected cohort to be silent. Do not diagnose outages from raw `ops.run_log` counts; Friday/Saturday zero-row days are expected under `daily_sun_thu` (`dow NOT IN (6,7)`, `ops/cadence.yaml`). Record a verified gap via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)`, never a new alert category; `ops.sp_sq_cadence_check` already owns `missed_run` via `state.cadence_watch`.
- **Upstream-output FRESHNESS check (W4 research handoff plus M4 / Q4 / A3 action-conversion routines) — REWRITTEN 2026-08-10, primary signal changed from marker-equality to the period-aware `ops.run_log` read `sp_assert_deps` already performs; origin: W4's own 2026-08-09 self-referral.** Use the period-aware dependency signal below. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-21.)*

  **PRIMARY signal, for every upstream this routine already declares as a dependency: the SAME `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('<ID>', <deps>, <today>)` the Dependency gate bullet above already requires before `sp_routine_start` — no new call, no new arithmetic.** In `bigquery/114_period_aware_dependency_gate.sql`, `dep_win` accepts ANY `completed` `ops.run_log` row in the DOWNSTREAM's current period: `weekly_sun` (W1/W2/W3) spans `DATE_SUB(in_run_date, INTERVAL (EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM in_run_date) - 1) DAY)` through today; `monthly_ftd` / `quarterly_ftd` / `annual_ftd` (M1b/M2/M3, Q2/Q3, A1/A2) span `DATE_TRUNC(in_run_date, MONTH/QUARTER/YEAR)` through today. The `ever` CTE self-bootstraps: no upstream run-log history means SATISFIED; after completions exist it becomes a real gate. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-22.)*

  **WHY THE MARKER CANNOT BE THE PROOF ON ITS OWN — the weekly Mon-vs-Sun anchor mismatch.** Keep marker checking only as corroborating shape/period sanity: ISO-week `YYYY-Www` markers (`scripts/check_cadence_marker.py`, `expected_marker()` / `d.isocalendar()`) are Monday-anchored, whereas `weekly_sun` dependencies (`dep_win`, `ops/cadence.yaml`) are Sunday-anchored, so fresh and stale cycles can share a marker. Still read the file's first line and check expected shape/period under the retrospective-offset rule below. Do not infer freshness from a marker match, or a missing dependency from a mismatch when `sp_assert_deps` passed; the latter is a separate stale-looking-output finding below.

  **FALLBACK, for any upstream genuinely not run-logged (dormant: every currently declared upstream is run-logged; retained for a future upstream that has not yet adopted run-logging).** Resolve the artifact's own git commit timestamp within the current period, using the identical resolution `scripts/check_cadence_marker.py`'s `write_dt()` already implements (lines 111-121): the newest commit touching the file in `merge-base(HEAD, origin/main)..HEAD` (falling back to `HEAD`'s own commit date for an uncommitted working-tree edit), converted to America/Denver, the pinned OPERATING plane — mirror it directly with `git log -1 --format=%aI -- <file>` (converted to America/Denver).

  (Be period-aware about the documented retrospective offset: Q1/Q3 and some monthly retrospectives legitimately carry the *prior* period marker — accept the prior period for those, per "File-write conventions". W4 → W1/W2/W3 current `YYYY-WW`; M4 → M1b/M2/M3; Q4 → Q2/Q3; A3 → A1/A2.)

  On a PRIMARY `sp_assert_deps` RAISE or a FALLBACK git-timestamp miss for an upstream without run-log history, apply the SAME DEPENDENCY-WAIT WINDOW: within one ~60-min window, poll every ~10 min, refresh the upstream file from `origin`'s current tip, re-`CALL ops.sp_assert_deps(...)`, and re-check the double-run guard each poll. If exhausted, state that in the alert. The primary call already alerts before RAISE: do not duplicate it. Otherwise `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('critical','<ID>','missing_dependency','<which upstream is stale/absent — signal used, value found vs expected>', '<JSON>')`. Log `'halted'` and ABORT; never convert stale research into orders. BigQuery/`alert_emailer.gs` delivers the finding, so no calendar event.

  **A corroborating marker/shape mismatch found DESPITE `sp_assert_deps` passing is deliberately NOT folded into the missing-dependency abort above (corrected 2026-08-10, same-day adversarial review of this rewrite — the paragraph above previously listed the marker mismatch as a third abort trigger, directly contradicting the WHY-THE-MARKER-CANNOT-BE-THE-PROOF paragraph above that (three paragraphs up from here) which already calls such a mismatch "not proof-by-itself of a missing dependency").** Raise `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','<ID>','upstream_marker_mismatch','<upstream> marker <found> does not match the expected <expected> for the current period, though ops.run_log shows it completed in-period — verify the file content is genuinely current, not merely its label', '<JSON: upstream, found_marker, expected_marker, run_log_row>')` and PROCEED. Do not halt or enter the DEPENDENCY-WAIT WINDOW for this alone; marker sanity follows `scripts/check_cadence_marker.py`. Keep this category ABSENT from `ops.alert_policy`: resolve by evidence, never age. Raise-time MUST populate `payload.upstream`. On a later run of THIS routine that verifies the SAME upstream's expected marker, best-effort `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note='marker re-verified: <upstream> now stamps <found> == expected <expected>, <ID> run <today>' WHERE category='upstream_marker_mismatch' AND NOT resolved AND JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.upstream') = '<upstream>'`; never blanket-clear the category. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-23.)*

- **A PROCEDURE THAT PASSED THE CI DRY-RUN HAS NOT BEEN SHOWN TO RUN — SMOKE-CALL IT AFTER APPLYING IT LIVE (added 2026-10-04, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing OPS1's `procedure_body_unvalidated_until_first_call`, alert `c93a7bcb-bce1-464f-8c8e-722de76d4669`; binds ANY session that lands a `CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE`).** The applying session must `CALL` the changed procedure once before `completed`, in that same session, and name the outcome in `<note>`. Use its no-op/idempotent path (`sp_raise_*`/`sp_sq_*` dedup/self-heal); for non-idempotent effects run its body's `SELECT`/`INSERT … SELECT` halves standalone or use a read-only/zero argument. On error fix via a new numbered file or `CREATE OR REPLACE` the prior body before session end. Do not add CI procedure calls: the post-apply smoke call owns runtime validation; revisit only after another measured omission.
- **Failure alerts (on any hard-stop).** Routine chat is unmonitored: a halt or need for a human requires `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('critical', '<ID>', '<category>', '<one-line message>', '<JSON context>')` AND run status `'halted'`; `alert_emailer.gs` polls every 2 hours, so no calendar event except the BigQuery-unreachable pre-flight above. `ops.sp_log_run` also raises `routine_run_failed` at `'warning'` on `'failed'`/`'halted'` (`bigquery/230_run_outcome_notification.sql`); never make that backstop critical, because open criticals feed the `blocking_criticals` term inside `state.trading_enabled` (`bigquery/176_decouple_embedding_health_from_trading_gate.sql`). The routine's own cause-specific diagnosis alert remains REQUIRED. Hard-stops include >$1 unexplained §13 cash residual (`cash_tripwire`), Strategy C closed-form/Monte-Carlo max-loss disagreement (`dual_path`), required IBKR/BigQuery unavailable (`connector`), D3 missed confirmation (`missed_confirmation`), and other unrecoverable state. Normal deferral to `conservative_default` is not a hard-stop. Embedding unhealthiness is not a hard-stop: call `ops.sp_embed_pending()` once best-effort and continue; persistent lag already surfaces as non-blocking `staleness`, and a new critical would re-latch trading. A hard-stop still owes Session end before its terminal row: commit changes, push the assigned branch and verify via `git ls-remote`, as for `completed`; only status and `error_msg` differ. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/00_preamble.md` § H-PRE-24.)*

- **IN-RUN ISSUE REPORTING — a run that COMPLETES but hit a problem.** For a completed run's warning/error, use `CALL ops.sp_report_run_issue('<ID>', <today>, '<issue_key>', '<summary>', '<JSON>')` (`bigquery/230_run_outcome_notification.sql`) to notify the unmonitored-chat operator. The procedure fixes severity at `'warning'`; it cannot halt trading. Genuine hard-stops use Failure alerts with their own diagnostic category (`missing_dependency`, `trading_halted`, `connector`, `bq_quota_exhausted`, etc.).

  **BEST-EFFORT, NEVER GATES — same posture as Run logging and Alert auto-resolve above (fixed 2026-09-08; a real defect until now).** `sp_report_run_issue` RAISEs on blank/whitespace or >64-character `<issue_key>`, or `<summary>` with fewer than 30 non-blank characters. Copy this wrapper verbatim:
  ```
  BEGIN
    CALL ops.sp_report_run_issue('<ID>', <today>, '<issue_key>', '<summary>', '<JSON>');
  EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN SELECT @@error.message;  -- swallow: a REFUSED validation floor must never abort the routine
  END;
  ```
  A REFUSED never halts the run: improve the key/summary and retry best-effort; if not retried, the run still completes. Never relax either validation floor to silence REFUSED: substantive reports require substantive text.

  `<issue_key>` names the KIND of issue, never the instance — it IS the `sp_raise_alert_once` dedup key folded into the alert message (`'fmp_rate_limited'`, never `'fmp_rate_limited_at_14:32'`); an instance-keyed value re-mints a fresh alert, and a fresh email, on every occurrence — the identical defect class `item_key` in bigquery/229_staged_order_confirm_notice.sql was written to avoid.
