**MODEL-OF-RECORD DOC SYNC (cadence audit 2026-07-29).** Read `ops/cadence.yaml`'s top-level `routine_model` key (corroborate against `OWNER_ACTIONS.md`; a live `RemoteTrigger` read wins over both if available; if that live read shows a fleet trigger whose model differs from `routine_model`, that is the `fleet_model_drift` condition — raise it per Q4 step E's FLEET-MODEL DRIFT bullet rather than silently preferring either side), then read the in-use-Claude-version field at `AI_Trading_Foundation.md`'s document head and its Part 4 restatement — the two sites Part 4's "Write authority — two tiers" subsection calls **Tier M**. **If both document sites already equal `routine_model`: do nothing.** No edit, no revision bump, no decision-log entry, no alert — this is the overwhelmingly common case, and it costs exactly two string comparisons. **If either document site differs from `routine_model`** — including the case where the two document sites merely disagree with EACH OTHER while one of them already matches `routine_model`: that disagreement is itself drift to repair, not a case to leave alone, since there must be exactly one correct value at both sites — proceed as follows.

**LAST-MOMENT RE-CHECK (shrinks the concurrent-writer collision window, cadence audit 2026-07-29 fix).** D3, Q4, and A3 can all reach this step, each on its own branch reset from `origin/main` at session start; two sessions whose runs overlap — which an OPS0/OPS2 catch-up refire can genuinely cause — can both read the field as stale before either writes, and there is no `merge=union` driver for `.md` files, so the second writer could encounter a conflict on the document-head revision number and appended revision-history bullet while updating its own PR. So immediately before making the edit below — not merely at session start — perform a **NON-DESTRUCTIVE** re-check: `git fetch origin`, then read the in-use-Claude-version field at both sites via `git show origin/main:AI_Trading_Foundation.md` — read that output only. **Never** do this with `git reset --hard origin/main` (the only concrete "refresh from origin" mechanism this document specifies anywhere — see the "Branch and state propagation" preamble) or any other command that touches the working tree: a Tier-M writer may be holding unrelated uncommitted edits to this same file, and **A3 in particular always is** — its own Section A applies up to five bullets of Tier-J KEEP/UPDATE/VERSION-PENDING/REMOVAL/NEW edits to `AI_Trading_Foundation.md` before ever reaching its own Tier-M bullet, and a destructive reset would discard that in-progress work. If another Tier-M writer has already synced it in the interim, NO-OP and exit this step right here: no edit, no revision bump, no decision-log entry, no alert. Otherwise make the edit and commit + push IMMEDIATELY following this re-check, so the window between the last read and the commit stays as small as possible: update the in-use-Claude-version field at BOTH sites so both equal `routine_model`, recording its sourcing the same way A3 already does; flip ALL Tier-2-tagged numerical claims to version-pending-replication UNCONDITIONALLY, with no carve-outs (Part 4 step 4 — a writer that updates the field MUST perform this flip in the SAME edit; splitting the two would leave capital-affecting Tier 2 magnitudes un-flagged while the field itself already reads the new model). **Scope the flip by the header-bracket tag ONLY** — the literal `[Tier 2` (or a bare `[Tier 2]`) in an item's `### N.N Title [...]` header — **NEVER** by scanning an item's body for existing "VERSION-PENDING" text; **replace ONLY the blockquote paragraph beginning `> **VERSION-PENDING REPLICATION**`**, never any other paragraph in the same block. This rule is structural, not enumerative: items currently carrying such a second blockquote paragraph — A1-authored **Tier-J** fade-review content, each beginning "A1's per-item fade review..." — include **1.3, 1.7, 2.4, 2.14, 2.15, and 2.19**; leave that second paragraph untouched on these items and on any other item that carries one, because overwriting or removing it would destroy Tier-J judgment content under cover of this Tier-M edit. **Item 2.21 is `[Tier 1]`-tagged only** but carries an unrelated `> **VERSION-PENDING (figures only)**` blockquote for a citation-integrity reason — it must NOT be touched by this flip; it is the worked example of why the header tag, not a body text-scan, is the determinant (Part 4's write-authority subsection). Then run `ops/foundation_change_review.md` §C "Model-version change" and write its required completion record via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` with `entry_type='foundation-change-review'`; increment `AI_Trading_Foundation.md`'s revision number and append a revision-history entry documenting the sync; and `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('info','D3','model_of_record_synced', '<old value> -> <new value> — in-use-Claude-version field synced from ops/cadence.yaml routine_model at both document-head and Part 4 sites; new_value is read directly from routine_model at write time (not independently derived) and old_value is the field\'s value immediately before this write, so a reader can sanity-check both against ops/cadence.yaml and the prior revision without digging. Committed and pushed on this session\'s branch; landing on main follows the own-PR publication protocol and is NOT asserted here as already live. Confirm the selected PR and main ancestry before claiming landing; if publication remains blocked, leave the PR intact and report its status. D3 re-checks the still-stale field on its next daily run. All Tier 2 claims flagged version-pending-replication.', '<JSON: old_value, new_value, source="ops/cadence.yaml routine_model">')`. Commit + push per §Branch and state propagation.

**Explicit Tier-J prohibition.** D3 must NOT touch item text, KEEP/UPDATE/VERSION-PENDING/REMOVAL/NEW dispositions, new numbered items, or any `Strategy.md` constraint change — that machinery stays A3-only, per Part 4's Tier-J boundary. If the model change turns out to have capability-research consequences, that is A1's (or Q3's) work on its own cadence, not D3's here: per Part 4 step 1, no early capability refresh fires off a version change — only the deployment fact syncs immediately; the research does not.

**Why D3 hosts this.** D3 runs every calendar day including non-trading days, is `catchup_safe: true`, and this is structurally the same read-signal -> self-edit -> commit shape as the MONITOR-PROMOTION SELF-FLIP block directly above. **Caveat — this step sits behind D3's own FATAL `sp_assert_deps('D3', ['D2'])` gate (Dependency gate, above), the same exposure D3's existing self-heal machinery already accepts (Known accepted limitation, OPS0 WATCHDOG-FALLBACK, above):** on a day D2 does not complete, D3 aborts before ever reaching this step, so the sync simply does not run that day. This is confirmed, not hypothetical — on 2026-07-25, D2 halted once (17:21:53 MDT) and D3 halted twice behind it (02:55:11 and 18:36:46 MDT); both self-healed not "the next morning" but **post-midnight the same operational night** — D2 completed at 00:50:25 MDT and D3 at 01:14:14 MDT, both on 2026-07-26 — which the routines' own `ops.run_log` notes describe as "midnight-crossing" / "post-midnight fire," not a next-morning recovery (a distinction that is load-bearing here, since post-midnight vs. morning is exactly what the SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD's noon threshold turns on). Do not overstate the exposure: it normally self-heals within a day via D3's own catch-up (`catchup_safe: true` + OPS0 refire), and even on a genuine compound-outage day the sync merely lands at the next successful D3, with Q4 (quarterly) and A3 (annual) standing behind it as the longer-horizon backstops.

**CI-FINDINGS ADJUDICATION & LIVE-SQL-PARITY SELF-HEAL (consumption-closure audit 2026-07-16; UNIFIED 2026-07-17 per OWNER_ACTIONS §I — the `ops.ci_findings` bridge is the single delivery path now that its `gh-ci-runner@` `bigquery.dataEditor` write grant is live [applied 2026-07-17], so the former separate JSON-file self-heal path [`ops/monitoring/live_sql_parity_findings.json`] is RETIRED and its latch/bounding/non-convergence safety folded in here — there is exactly one live-sql-parity self-heal path now, not two).** `SELECT * FROM state.ci_findings_open` (bigquery/67_ci_findings_bridge.sql).

Rows with finding_key `keyless_sa`/`wif_binding`/`guard_config` are owner-remediation classes (IAM/console/secrets): take no repair action; the `ci_finding` warning alert already delivers them to the monitored email channel.

Rows with `workflow='stranded-branch-check'` (finding_key `stranded_branch`) are a GIT-SIDE class, added 2026-08-09 when stranded-branch-check.yml — the last CI guard still delivering only to a GitHub issue — was wired to the `ops.ci_findings` bridge. **Take no repair action here, and do NOT route these into the live-SQL self-heal branches below** — the finding_key is a fixed literal, not a `<dataset>.<object>`, so there is nothing to re-apply or create, and the condition is not in BigQuery at all. It means a routine logged `completed` in `ops.run_log` while its committed output never reached `main` (RUNBOOK §20): a branch with failed or incomplete publication checks, a missing selected-PR dispatch, or an unresolved PR conflict. `detail` names the branches/PRs. The `ci_finding` warning alert now delivers it to the monitored email channel, and the workflow auto-resolves its own row on the next clean 8-hourly sweep. **Why this producer exists at all:** on 2026-08-08/09 one dbt-parity drift turned CI red on EVERY branch touching `bigquery/**`|`dbt/**`, so auto-merge (which drains only green branches) stranded BOTH open branches and `main` fell behind live. This workflow detected it correctly and filed an issue, but being the one guard off the bridge, the ROOT CAUSE was invisible on the alert channel while its downstream symptoms were not. Treat a firing of this category as a LANDING-PIPELINE outage, not a per-branch nuisance: check whether ONE shared gate is red across every branch (`gh pr list --state open` returning nothing while branch CI is red is the tell) before triaging branches individually. Remediate a shared gate defect on this session's OWN assigned branch, publish its own PR through §Branch and state propagation, and report the other affected branches/PRs. Do not update or adopt another in-use branch; its owning session must refresh from main and regenerate affected slices, unless the owner explicitly selects one exact branch/tip for the guarded OPS0 recovery checklist.

**RETIRED PRODUCER (2026-08-30) — this class can only ever be adjudicating a HISTORICAL row now; keep the guidance below for exactly that case.** `gemini-key-health.yml` (the sole producer of `workflow='gemini-key-health'` rows) was deleted 2026-08-30 together with `golden-prose-daily.yml`, the only functional consumer of `GEMINI_API_KEY` in this repo's CI (removed for cost + a measured-zero-precision prose-regression signal — see `.github/workflows/golden-scenarios.yml`'s header for the evidence trail). With no producer left, **no NEW `gemini_key_dead` row can ever arrive**; if D3 sees one it is necessarily a pre-2026-08-30 row still sitting open in `ops.ci_findings`. Adjudicate any such row exactly as before — the guidance was correct then and remains correct for a stale row now, it just no longer has a live producer behind it:

Rows with `workflow='gemini-key-health'` (finding_key `gemini_key_dead`) are an OWNER-REMEDIATION class, added 2026-08-19 with the `gemini-key-health.yml` producer (a daily `models.list` probe of `GEMINI_API_KEY`). **Take no repair action here, and do NOT route these into the live-SQL self-heal branches below** — the finding_key is a fixed literal, not a `<dataset>.<object>`, there is nothing in BigQuery to re-apply or create, and the only fix is a human minting a new key in Google AI Studio, which no routine can do. It means the key was rejected with HTTP 401/403, so `golden-scenarios.yml`'s advisory live job was silently blind at the time (it was `continue-on-error`, so it kept reporting SUCCESS while every scenario errored) — that live job no longer exists either (retired 2026-08-30), so this consequence is now historical too. `detail` carries the status code and points at **`OWNER_ACTIONS.md` item `G-authkey`**, which is the actual remediation (that item is unaffected by this producer's retirement — it now also carries a 2026-08-30 note asking the owner whether `G-authkey` itself is still needed, since the key has no functional CI consumer left; that is a separate open question, not something this adjudication step decides). Since the producer is gone, no future probe will auto-resolve a lingering row — if a pre-2026-08-30 row is still open, adjudicate it by hand once against `OWNER_ACTIONS.md` `G-authkey`'s current status rather than waiting for a self-resolve that can no longer happen. **A 429 was NOT this condition** — the probe treated a rate-limited response as ALIVE, because it proved the credential authenticated; a `gemini_key_dead` row meant the key really was rejected. **Its known blind spot, for context on any historical row:** the probe proved the key was alive on the day it ran and could not tell a legacy Standard (`AIza`) key from an auth (`AQ.`) key, so a key later rejected outright at Google's September 2026 Standard-key cutoff would have probed perfectly healthy right up to the deadline. That migration is `G-authkey`'s job, not this row's.

Rows with `workflow='b3-invariants'` (finding_key `b3_invariants`) are a LIVE-DATA class, added 2026-07-30 when the B3 invariant suite (`dbt test`) moved off ci.yml's push trigger onto live-sql-parity.yml's daily job. **Take no repair action here, and do NOT route these into the live-SQL self-heal branches below** — the finding_key is a test-suite name, not a `<dataset>.<object>`, so there is nothing to re-apply or create. What failed is an assertion about live DATA (a reserved_cash formula mismatch, a queue latest-wins violation, a duplicated `daily_marks` day, a health view that stopped returning exactly one row), which needs diagnosis of the writer that produced the data, not a DDL re-apply. The `ci_finding` warning alert delivers it to the monitored email channel, and the producing workflow auto-resolves its own row on the next clean daily run. Investigate the named failing test(s) in `detail` as an ordinary triage item; if the cause turns out to be a genuine repo-side defect, fix it through the normal branch-and-push path, not through this step's self-heal machinery.

For each `workflow='live-sql-parity'` row: since 2026-07-18 the workflow writes ONE ROW PER DRIFTED OBJECT, and since 2026-07-28 (owner directive — autonomous creation of a declared-but-absent object now authorized, no human approval step) it ALSO writes one row per genuinely MISSING object. `finding_key` is the `<dataset>.<name>` of the live BigQuery object either way; the two classes are told apart by an explicit marker at the START of `detail` — a row whose `detail` begins literally `MISSING: ` (`scripts/check_live_sql_parity.py`'s `missing_objects` category) means the object does not exist live at all and is handled by branch **(d)** below; every other row is ordinary drift, `detail` names its canonical source file, and is handled by branches (a)/(b)/(c) below. The view's `first_detected` (bigquery/86) is that object's own episode start, computed identically for both classes. (A row with the legacy aggregate `finding_key='live_sql_parity'` means the parity run could not verify anything — checker fail-closed, zero per-object data: treat as an environment/workflow problem, not object drift or absence; no action.) Act only on a finding that has PERSISTED across >= 2 daily parity runs — skip an object whose finding `first_detected` is today (the one-day lag deliberately gives a same-day out-of-band live hotfix time to land its repo commit per the bigquery/47 discipline before being reverted; for a MISSING finding specifically, see branch (d)'s rail 1 for why this matters even more there). Take at most 10 objects per session ACROSS (a) AND (d) COMBINED (not 10 of each), oldest `first_detected` first (bounded blast radius; the rest drain on subsequent days). For each such object:

- **LATCH CHECK first (applies to BOTH classes — a drift re-apply and a (d) MISSING create):** `SELECT dataset, object FROM ops.parity_selfheal_log WHERE heal_date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver'), INTERVAL 7 DAY)` (bigquery/69_live_sql_parity_selfheal.sql — `heal_date` is the OPERATING-plane trading-day key, so read and write it with the Denver qualifier, never the bare unqualified form, which is UTC and rolls over mid-evening Denver; its sibling `first_detected` is Denver-planed too) — if this object was healed within 7 days and is STILL flagged (drifted or MISSING), the heal is not converging (comparator bug, a competing live writer, or for a MISSING object a create that silently didn't take): do NOT re-apply and do NOT create; instead `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D3','live_sql_parity_selfheal_ineffective','<dataset.object> re-flagged after a self-heal within 7d — NOT re-applying/re-creating; comparator or competing-writer investigation needed','<JSON: object, source_file, first_detected, prior heal_date, prior_outcome>')` and leave the GitHub issue open for the owner.
- Otherwise check the finding's `detail`: if it begins with the `MISSING: ` marker, this is **(d)**, handled below with its own rails. Every other row is drift — read the live definition (INFORMATION_SCHEMA.VIEWS / .ROUTINES) and the repo final-effective definition and adjudicate: **(a)** live body is stale/clobbered → re-apply the repo definition verbatim via the BigQuery MCP respecting bigquery/README.md apply order; for a VIEW run `SELECT 1 FROM <object> LIMIT 1` as a compile check; `INSERT INTO ops.parity_selfheal_log (heal_date, dataset, object, source_file, first_detected, outcome) VALUES (CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver'), ..., 'applied')` (on a re-apply error instead `INSERT ... 'failed'`, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D3','live_sql_parity_selfheal_failed','<dataset.object> — self-heal apply failed; see payload for the error','<JSON>')`, and leave the finding — the workflow's GitHub issue stays open) (message identity is object name only; job/timestamp-varying error text goes in payload; branch (d) uses the same fixed literal). **(b)** live body is a legitimate not-yet-committed hotfix → commit it as a new `bigquery/NN_*_resync.sql` (the bigquery/47 precedent) and push (auto-merge on green CI). **(c)** live and repo already MATCH in meaning → take NO apply action and write NO `parity_selfheal_log` row (nothing was healed by this session); before concluding, attribute via `region-us.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT` `user_email`/`statement_type` for recent DDL on the object (check who applied before attributing) and note the attribution in the decision_log entry; the next daily parity run auto-resolves the finding. When deciding between (a)/(b)/(c), compare MEANING, not formatting — BigQuery re-serializes stored definitions (comments stripped, backticks dropped, quote style normalized; `scripts/check_live_sql_parity.py`'s `canonicalize()` is the reference for what counts as a real difference). NEVER re-apply a TABLE object.
- **(d) MISSING — the object does not exist live at all (autonomous creation authorized, NO human approval step; `scripts/check_live_sql_parity.py` documents the superseded missing-object exclusion).** The compensating control here is the set of mechanical rails below, not human review — consistent with this repo's standing SISA posture (CLAUDE.md) that compensating controls are mechanical rails, not a review gate. Run the DROP-GUARD (rail 4, below) FIRST; if it clears, CREATE the object verbatim from the repo's final-effective `bigquery/*.sql` definition (respecting `bigquery/README.md` apply order) via the BigQuery MCP; for a VIEW run the same `SELECT 1 FROM <object> LIMIT 1` compile check branch (a) uses; `INSERT INTO ops.parity_selfheal_log (heal_date, dataset, object, source_file, first_detected, outcome) VALUES (CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver'), ..., 'created')` (on a create error instead `INSERT ... 'failed'`, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D3','live_sql_parity_selfheal_failed','<dataset.object> — self-heal apply failed; see payload for the error','<JSON>')` — the same failure category branch (a) uses, since both are "a self-heal attempt failed," and leave the finding — the workflow's GitHub issue stays open). NEVER create a TABLE object (rail 5). Log `events.decision_log` the same as the other branches (`entry_type='ci-finding-adjudication'`), noting explicitly that this was a CREATE of a previously-absent object, not a re-apply. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D3.md` § H-D3-04.)*

  RAILS FOR (d) — the existing rails above apply unchanged, plus one new one:
  1. The EXISTING >=2-daily-run persistence rule (in the paragraph introducing this step, above) applies unchanged — skip an object whose `first_detected` is today. It matters MORE here than for a drift re-apply: this is exactly the window in which someone lands a new `bigquery/NN_*.sql` file and applies it live minutes later (the normal, expected lag between a repo commit and its out-of-band MCP/console apply — `bigquery/README.md`'s own apply model) — creating the object here, underneath them, would race that landing instead of letting it happen, the mirror image of why the same one-day lag exists for a drift finding.
  2. The EXISTING 7-day LATCH CHECK (above) applies unchanged: if this object was already healed (created OR re-applied) within 7 days and is STILL absent, do NOT create it again — `live_sql_parity_selfheal_ineffective` fires instead, exactly as it would for a non-converging drift re-apply.
  3. The EXISTING bound of at most 10 objects per session applies ACROSS (a) and (d) COMBINED, not 10 of each — restated above in the paragraph introducing this step.
  4. **NEW MECHANICAL DROP-GUARD (2026-07-28) — the important one.** Before creating, `grep` every `bigquery/*.sql` file for a top-level `DROP` statement naming this exact `<dataset>.<name>` (mirroring `scripts/check_live_sql_parity.py`'s own `DROP_STMT` pattern — `DROP (MATERIALIZED VIEW|TABLE FUNCTION|VIEW|TABLE|PROCEDURE|FUNCTION) [IF EXISTS] <project>.<dataset>.<name>`, backticks optional per identifier segment). If ANY file drops it, do NOT create it — instead `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D3','live_sql_parity_missing_but_dropped','<dataset.object> reported MISSING by live-sql-parity, but <dropping file> DROPs it — NOT creating; treating as a deliberately retired object','<JSON: object, source_file, dropping_file>')` and stop for this object (leave its `ci_findings` row open — do not resolve it yourself). RATIONALE: `find_final_definitions()` already resolves `CREATE`/`DROP` in textual apply order to build its own expected-object set, and that resolution is exactly why a genuinely-retired object (e.g. `bigquery/92`'s park-allocator views, whose own header says "DO NOT re-create live — 108 drops it") normally never reaches this branch at all — it drops out of the expected set entirely and is reported neither as drift nor as missing. But if that parser's own DROP-resolution logic is ever wrong (a future regex edit, an unanticipated statement form), the object would wrongly look absent-but-still-expected, and this branch would silently RESURRECT something deliberately removed. This grep is an INDEPENDENT second check — it does not reuse or depend on `find_final_definitions()`'s own ordering/resolution logic at all, so a bug in that one parser cannot by itself cause an irreversible live CREATE; the two checks would both have to be wrong in the same way for a resurrection to slip through.
  5. NEVER create a TABLE object (mirrors branch (a)'s existing NEVER-re-apply-a-TABLE rule).
- Either way log `events.decision_log` (`CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)`, `entry_type='ci-finding-adjudication'`, object + which side won + why). Do NOT write the ops.ci_findings resolved row yourself — the next daily parity run confirms and closes it.

Never a chat question.

**UNWIRED-MONITOR BRIDGE (resilience audit 2026-07-16 — self-retiring; covers bigquery/64/65's checks and cadence_check's own body-version drift while/whenever the live cadence_check body is not current, OWNER_ACTIONS.md §B).** `SELECT monitored, drift FROM state.scheduled_query_version_drift WHERE sq_name='cadence_check'`. If `monitored = TRUE AND drift = FALSE` (the live cadence_check body is current, so its own in-query versions of these checks are running), SKIP the rest of this bullet entirely — it exists only for the stale-body window. Otherwise: (i) if `monitored = TRUE AND drift = TRUE` (cadence_check itself regressed — a regressed body cannot self-report), `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D3','scheduled_query_version_drift', CONCAT('Scheduled-query body drift: live body running an unexpected/regressed version: cadence_check (expected ', expected_version, ', reported ', COALESCE(last_reported_version,'NONE'), ')'), '<TO_JSON_STRING of the row>')`; (ii) if `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM state.b3_trading_enabled_check WHERE drift)`, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D3','b3_trading_enabled_drift', 'B3 trading-enabled drift — the live gate disagrees with its expected value; see payload for live_value and expected_value', '<TO_JSON_STRING of the row>')`; (iii) if `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM state.backup_per_table_health WHERE row_count_dropped)`, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D3','backup_per_table_row_drop', '<dataset-tables> — per-table row-count drop detected in the backup; see payload for the per-table counts (DISTINCT, ASCENDING, comma-joined, no spaces)', '<TO_JSON_STRING of the rows>')`. Same category strings as cadence_check's own blocks, so the downstream alert/email path is identical; sp_raise_alert_once dedups on unresolved (category, message) and the bridge stops firing entirely once the re-paste lands, so nothing double-fires post-paste.

**APPLY-LAG EXCLUSION ON (i) — A BODY THAT IS CURRENT BUT HAS NOT BEATEN SINCE IT WAS APPLIED IS NOT A REGRESSION (added 2026-09-08, D3, measured on this run).** `state.scheduled_query_version_drift.drift` is a bare equality test between the registry's `expected_version` and the version carried by the LAST HEARTBEAT (`bigquery/111`: `monitored AND (last_reported_version IS NULL OR TRIM(...) = '' OR last_reported_version != e.expected_version)`) — it had **no grace term at all** when this paragraph was written; the GRACE_FACTOR of 1.5 in that same view guards `stale_beat` and `never_beat_overdue` only, and neither feeds this clause. **PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-09-23, D3, measured live against `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.VIEWS` this run — THE VIEW ITSELF NOW CARRIES THIS GRACE AND HAS SINCE 2026-09-09, ONE DAY AFTER THIS PARAGRAPH LANDED.** `bigquery/232_sq_version_drift_bootstrap_grace.sql` (commit `37cf0d3`, 2026-09-09) added the conjunct `lb.last_beat_ts >= COALESCE(e.updated_ts, TIMESTAMP '1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC')` to the `drift` expression, so `drift` is now FALSE by construction until the query has beaten at least once since its `state.expected_scheduled_query_versions` row was bumped — which IS the apply-lag case this paragraph was written to work around, closed structurally at the source. That file's own header cites the SAME incident this paragraph does (alert `e0cb2898`, `fire_drill_alert_lifecycle`, registry v4 2026-09-08, live DDL v4, heartbeat v3 from 2026-09-01), so the two are the same finding fixed twice — once in D3 prose, once in the view — and only the view's half was ever load-bearing. **MEASURED THIS RUN, the live proof the conjunct is active:** `fire_drill_alert_lifecycle` reads `expected_version` v4 against `last_reported_version` v3 (last beat 2026-09-01, monthly cadence) and `drift = FALSE` — a bare equality test would read TRUE there. **So treat the positive-evidence suppression below as a fail-closed BACKSTOP, not as the primary mechanism, and do NOT delete it on the strength of this correction:** it costs one live-body read on the rare evenings `drift = TRUE` at all, its asymmetry argument is independently sound, and a future edit to `bigquery/232`'s conjunct would silently re-open the hole with nothing else watching. What must NOT survive is the factual claim that the view has no grace term — a session reading that against the live definition would conclude the view is broken when it is not. The heartbeat is written when the procedure RUNS, and `cadence_check` runs once daily at 05:15 UTC, so on any day a new `bigquery/NN_*.sql` is applied live AFTER that slot — which is exactly what the MONITOR-PROMOTION SELF-FLIP step above instructs D3 itself to do ("APPLY IT LIVE in this same session") — `drift` reads TRUE for up to ~24h on a body that is ALREADY CURRENT, purely because the last beat predates the apply. **MEASURED 2026-09-08:** `expected_version` v22, `last_reported_version` v21, last beat 2026-09-07 23:15 MT, `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.ROUTINES.last_altered` 2026-09-08 07:46 MT (`bigquery/230` applied live), and the live body's own literal `sp_beat_heartbeat('sq:cadence_check', 'v22', ...)` — i.e. the body was current and simply had not run since. Raising there is a false positive WITH TEETH: `scheduled_query_version_drift` is ABSENT from `ops.alert_policy`, so it LATCHES under the fail-closed default and only a human can ever clear it, for a condition that clears itself at the next 05:15 UTC beat.

**So before raising (i), read the live body and suppress ONLY on POSITIVE evidence that it is current — BOTH of these, together:** the `sp_beat_heartbeat('sq:cadence_check', '<ver>', ...)` version literal in `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.ROUTINES.routine_definition` EQUALS `expected_version`, **AND** that routine's `last_altered` is strictly LATER than `state.scheduled_query_version_drift.last_beat_ts`. State both readings and both timestamps in this run's `<note>` — suppressing on inference is how the once-it-matters case gets missed, so the suppression must leave a written trace, exactly as the queue-stale branch's clause (b)/(c) zero-count branches require. **THE ASYMMETRY IS THE ENTIRE SAFETY ARGUMENT, same shape as clause (c) of the OWNER-ELIGIBLE-DAY BRANCH above: only positive, fresh evidence of a current body suppresses, and nothing else ever does.** Three configurations must keep raising and this exclusion leaves all three untouched: **(1)** a genuinely REGRESSED or clobbered body — its heartbeat literal does NOT equal `expected_version` (the `bigquery/47` live-clobber class, which is what this clause exists for); **(2)** a body that was never re-applied after the registry was bumped — `last_altered < last_beat_ts`, so the repo moved and live did not; **(3)** a body whose version literal cannot be read at all — fail closed and raise. Only "current AND not yet beaten" is suppressed, and it self-clears within one beat. **Do NOT widen this into a bare age or grace window on `drift` itself** — a flat 24h grace would suppress a REAL regression for the same 24h, which is the opposite of what this clause is for; the discriminator must stay the live body's own version literal, never elapsed time. Checks (ii) and (iii) are unaffected and still run whenever `drift = TRUE`, since a suppressed (i) does not prove cadence_check's in-query siblings ran this cycle.

Walk all `[Claude]` events in the next 90 days. Under the 2026-07-09 policy the calendar should contain only the two exception-case events (a non-craftable order's manual-entry `[Claude] Confirm order`, or a `[Claude] ATTENTION — RE-AUTH BigQuery connector`):
- Any OTHER `[Claude]` event still present — a legacy analysis event (thesis construction, re-screen, research-deferral checkpoint, foundation-change assessment, constraint-relaxation review, router review, pulse-check / time-exit / convergence check) or a craftable-order confirm-order event left over from before this policy — is stale: for a legacy analysis event, convert it to a `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entry (`INSERT INTO events.queue_events`) with an appropriate `due_date` + self-contained `context` (or, for pulse / time-exit / convergence checks, simply drop it — D1's daily mechanical exit sweep covers those), then delete the calendar event; for a leftover craftable confirm-order event, just delete it once Step 0 / the missed-order check above confirms the underlying order is filled/cancelled/reconciled — its human-facing job was already done by the IBKR notification.
- For a genuine **manual-entry confirm-order event** (non-craftable order): DELETE it only when its order day has passed AND the order has been entered/filled or cancelled per Step 0 reconciliation. DO NOT delete it solely because its datetime is past and unconfirmed — fold it into the MISSED-ENTRY/EXIT CHECK above (it is a `state.open_orders` row like any other; the same `missed_confirmation` alert applies). Confirm its description carries a valid manual-entry text block + `SIDE QTY TICKER TYPE LIMIT TIF` summary + instruction `id`, and that the notification fires at event-time.
- For a `[Claude] ATTENTION — RE-AUTH BigQuery connector` event: delete it once the BigQuery connector is confirmed live again (this session's own pre-flight passing is sufficient evidence).

**TRADING-ENABLE GATE — D3 STAGES ORDERS TOO, SO IT NEEDS ITS OWN (added 2026-07-27, `INCIDENT[ref=423ecc02-fdb7-4f47-9445-d8c79d399e8c]`).** Before the walk below: `CALL ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()` (best-effort), then read NON-FATALLY `SELECT trading_enabled, halt_reason FROM state.trading_enabled`. If FALSE, apply the shared **PRE-REFRESH HALT DISPOSITION** rule above — read `state.staging_halt_disposition.gate_alert_action`; on `defer_to_craft_site` raise NOTHING here (the FALSE verdict and every craft block below stand unchanged) and defer the critical to the craft site that actually declines; on `raise_critical`, or if that column cannot be read, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('critical', 'D3', 'trading_halted', 'Order staging blocked: trading is HALTED. See payload for the triggering routine and reason.', TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT('D3' AS routine, <halt_reason> AS halt_reason)))`, carry the verdict forward as a session fact, and **CONTINUE** — the calendar hygiene, queue hygiene, attestation, alerting and reconciliation-flagging work below all proceed regardless. What a FALSE verdict blocks is narrow but real: **do NOT stage a NEW `ORDER_STAGED` row, and do NOT perform the GO-WITHOUT-ORDER re-stage** — record the omission via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` citing `halt_reason` and let D2 resurface the candidate when the gate clears. The daily persist-and-wait RE-CRAFT of an already-staged, already-owner-confirmed pending row is NOT blocked, for exactly the reasons D2a's gate paragraph gives: re-crafting re-issues an intent the registry already carries rather than adding exposure, and gating it would strand an exit and re-open the 2026-06-08 MDT de-funding failure.

**WHY D3 NEEDS THIS AT ALL — it was never protected on purpose.** D3 has always crafted orders here (`create_order_instruction` + `ORDER_STAGED` writes, the re-craft and re-stage bullets below) with no trading-enable check of its own; its only gate is the FATAL `sp_assert_deps('D3', ['D2'])` above. That gate blocked D3 during a halt purely as a SIDE EFFECT — D2 aborted, so D2 never logged `completed`, so D3's dependency gate RAISEd (live on 2026-07-25: D2 halted 17:21 MT, D3 halted 18:36 MT with `missing completed upstream: D2`). The moment D2 correctly completes through a halt instead of aborting — which is the whole point of the 2026-07-27 gate rework — that accidental protection disappears and D3 would happily stage orders while trading is halted. Protection that only works because an unrelated upstream crashed is not protection; it is a coincidence that was load-bearing. This paragraph replaces it with the real thing.

Walk staged orders from **`state.open_orders`** (the durable staged-order registry, Operating_Protocols.md §11 — the authoritative list of what is meant to be resting, since under DAY-only the live endpoints are empty between sessions) and open positions from `state.current_positions`, cross-checked against the connector (`get_account_positions`, `get_account_orders`, `get_order_instructions`). **Apply an explicit `COALESCE(item_type,'') <> 'drip-dust-liquidation'` filter to D3's missing-instruction repair, filled detection, daily re-craft, and generic window-expiry loops; D2a's exact-source dust procedure exclusively owns those rows and D3 must not create or terminal a duplicate.** D3 may report a malformed dust row but does not reconcile it:
- For every still-`pending` NON-DUST `state.open_orders` row (`COALESCE(item_type,'') <> 'drip-dust-liquidation'`), confirm it has a live crafted instruction in `get_order_instructions` matching its `payload.instruction_id` — and, if the underlying order is non-craftable, that its manual-entry confirm-order event also exists at 07:00 MT pre-market on the order day (if the order day is still in the future; craftable orders rely on `create_order_instruction`'s own IBKR notification instead, no event to check). **TAPPED IS NOT MISSING — CROSS-CHECK `get_account_orders` BEFORE TREATING AN INSTRUCTION AS LOST.** An absent instruction is NOT by itself evidence the craft was lost. `create_order_instruction` creates an *instruction, not a live order*, and the operator's confirm-tap CONSUMES it: the instruction drops off `get_order_instructions` and a working order appears in `get_account_orders`. PRE-FILL INVALIDATION RE-CHECK below turns on the same instruction-to-order transition. So before concluding "missing", read `get_account_orders` and look for a working order matching this row (same `contract_id`/ticker, side, and quantity). If one exists, the instruction was TAPPED: the row is correctly `pending` and resting for the next session, the persist-and-wait re-craft below does not apply either (its own precondition is a DAY order that *expired unfilled*, not one still working), and you must NOT re-craft. **A re-craft here would stage a SECOND order for exposure the first one already fully covers.**  Only when NEITHER an instruction NOR a matching working order exists is the craft genuinely lost: then, if the order day is still future, re-craft it (`create_order_instruction`) and repair the event (non-craftable only). If the order day is today and market is still open, create/repair the event immediately (non-craftable only). If the order day is past and the order was Day duration (now the only duration Claude crafts — Operating_Protocols.md §11), it either filled or expired — confirm via Step 0 reconciliation / `get_account_trades`; flag if not yet reconciled (if it expired unfilled but the thesis still wants the entry/exit, it is re-crafted as a fresh DAY order per the persist-and-wait re-craft step below).
  - **CONFIRM-EVENT ATTESTATION (non-craftable orders only; a craftable order's IBKR notification is gated by staging atomicity).** For a non-craftable `state.open_orders` row, the check above already repairs a missing confirm event in-session, but that leaves no durable record it happened. Before moving to the next such row, `INSERT INTO ops.confirm_event_snapshot` (snapshot_date, item_key, ticker, side, entry_window_close, confirm_event_found, calendar_event_id, repaired) recording the search result from the check above (`confirm_event_found` = whether one already existed; `calendar_event_id` = its id if found/created; `repaired = TRUE` if this run had to create or fix it). This does not change the repair logic — it makes "D3 verified confirm-event completeness today" independently queryable (`SELECT * FROM state.staged_without_confirm`) instead of implicit in D3's chat summary, so a D3 session that crashes before reaching this point, or a Calendar-connector write that silently fails, is visible to other monitors instead of surfacing only days later via the missed-confirmation hard-stop above. If `state.staged_without_confirm` returns any row at the START of this bullet (from a PRIOR D3 run — `flag_reason` = `never_attested` / `confirm_event_missing` / `attestation_stale`), `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D3','confirm_event_gap', '<item_key> — confirm-event gap: the staged order has no matching confirm event; see payload for the ticker and the flag reason', <JSON>)` (fixed message keyed on `item_key` only, one open row per gapped item) in addition to repairing it.
- **PRE-FILL INVALIDATION RE-CHECK. Runs BEFORE the garbage-collection and persist-and-wait re-craft bullets below, so an already-invalidated entry is neither re-crafted nor quietly left to fill.** A thesis is written and its order crafted in the evening block, but a MARKET/DAY order does not fill until the **next open** — 6–9 hours later, across which the sell-side reaction to the very event the thesis is built on is still printing. Re-evaluate recorded invalidation in this craft-to-fill window; D3 already walks these rows and can delete untapped instructions. This is the same idiom as D2 item 2a's add-candidate gate — *"Re-verify the hard gate first, same session (D1's read may be stale by the time D2 runs) … confirm they remain UNBREACHED as of today's data"* — applied one step earlier, to an order that has not filled yet rather than to an add on a position that already exists. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D3.md` § H-D3-05.)*

  For each still-`pending` NON-DUST (`COALESCE(item_type,'') <> 'drip-dust-liquidation'`) **entry** row whose order day is today or still future and which the walk above did not resolve as already filled (resting EXITS are deliberately out of scope — an exit that is still wanted is not made less wanted by adverse news, and D2/W3 own exit judgment):
  1. **Resolve the thesis and its recorded criteria** — `payload.source_decision_ref` → `events.decision_log`, plus the immutable criteria on the provisional `events.position_events` row's `invalidation_status` JSON.
  2. **Re-evaluate ONLY those recorded criteria** against information published SINCE the thesis timestamp — a bounded single-ticker check (analyst actions, company releases/guidance, halts), not a fresh thesis. Cheap by construction: this row set is normally 0–2.
  3. **If a criterion is already MET, the entry must not proceed.** Branch on whether the operator has tapped, which is mechanically observable because `create_order_instruction` creates an *instruction, not a live order*: an entry still listed by `get_order_instructions` with no matching live order in `get_account_orders` is **un-tapped**; once tapped it converts to a live order and drops off the instruction list.
     - **Un-tapped → PREVENT.** `delete_order_instruction(<payload.instruction_id>)`, set the `ORDER_STAGED` row terminal `abandoned` with a logged terminal decision, and NET OUT the staging-time provisional OPEN `events.position_events` row exactly as D2a's PHANTOM-CLOSE RULE does — the position never existed.
     - **Already tapped → CANNOT CANCEL.** The connector exposes no cancel-live-order call (only create/delete of *instructions*), so the order will fill. Leave it, and hand a same-session exit to the next D2 by logging the decision with the criterion and the evidence cited, so D2 stages the exit at its next run rather than waiting for the weekly W3 to rediscover it.
     - Either way: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('critical','D3','prefill_invalidation','<ticker> — a recorded invalidation criterion was met before the entry filled; <prevented|exit handed to D2>','<JSON: ticker, strategy, criterion, instruction_id, tapped>')` and `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` with `entry_type='prefill-invalidation'`.
  4. **NOT blocked by the TRADING-ENABLE gate.** Deleting an un-tapped instruction and netting out its provisional OPEN is not an order craft and creates no new exposure — it strictly REDUCES it, the conservative direction — so it proceeds on a FALSE verdict exactly as exit re-craft, kill-trigger termination and park cover already do (`bigquery/78`'s header requirement). A halt is a reason not to open a position; it is never a reason to let an already-invalidated one open.
  5. **Calibration honesty — this is NOT a losing thesis.** A prevented (or immediately-exited) entry of this class is a PROCESS outcome, not a strategy outcome: it must not enter the conviction-tier win-rate, the precedent-outcome annotations, or the 30-trade graduation counter as a thesis that lost. It is evidence about entry TIMING, not about the edge, and recording it as a loss would corrupt exactly the calibration series it should inform.
  6. **The re-check NEVER re-litigates the thesis on the merits.** It evaluates only the criteria the thesis itself recorded, mechanically — it cannot convert a GO to a NO-GO on fresh judgment, and a criterion not met leaves the order untouched and silent. That boundary is what keeps this a control rather than a second opinion, and it is also its known limit: invalidating news that no recorded criterion covers will not be caught here.

  Structural note for thesis authors and for SL/W5, NOT a gate here: a criterion keyed on sell-side CLUSTER formation is near-certain to fire when the thesis is written DURING the post-event analyst reaction window, because the cluster is still forming — the 2026-08-03 MTZ entry was written overnight on an "isolated dissenter" premise and had three further ≥15% price-target cuts land the next morning, one of them published before the fill. W3 2026-W32 independently proposed the corresponding entry-side question (whether negative-direction B entries need a minimum settling window of ~3 sessions post-event before an isolated-dissenter read can be trusted); that belongs to strategy design, not to this reconciliation step, and is left to that review.

- Garbage-collect stale crafted instructions: any `get_order_instructions` entry whose order day has passed unconfirmed, or whose position is already closed/opened per reconciliation, is cleared with `delete_order_instruction`.
  This garbage-collection loop also carries `COALESCE(item_type,'') <> 'drip-dust-liquidation'`; only D2a may delete or
  terminal a dust instruction.
- **Explicit scope for the next loop:** its iteration query MUST include
  `WHERE COALESCE(item_type,'') <> 'drip-dust-liquidation'`; every "still-pending row" below means a NON-DUST row.
- Daily re-craft of persist-and-wait orders (DAY-only policy, Operating_Protocols.md §11; primary path is the D2 Step 0 staged-order registry reconciliation — D3 is the calendar-side backstop): a Claude-crafted DAY order does not rest overnight — it fills or expires at session close — so an order meant to persist is kept alive by re-crafting it fresh each session; orders are MARKET, so a re-craft is simply a fresh market order on a fresh reference price, never a re-price of a resting limit. For each still-`pending` `state.open_orders` row whose prior DAY order expired unfilled but whose window is still open (`entry_window_close >= today` / exit still required): **Same boundary rule as D2a Step 0 branch (b): `entry_window_close = today` read post-close means the re-craft reaches the NEXT session S, so either advance the window to `>= S` or set the row terminal — never carry a now-past window forward (Operating_Protocols.md §11).** **ORDER-GUARD CHECK first, same as the D2 Step 0(b) primary path (required on this alternate path too; prevents `order_guard_omitted`) — `SELECT * FROM analytics.fn_order_guard(<strategy>, <side>, <qty>, <ref_price>, 'MARKET')` (or `fn_order_guard_options(<strategy>, <side>, <contracts>, <ref_premium>, <max_loss_dollars>, 'MARKET')` for an options leg — market-only + malformed-input sanity only, `bigquery/104_strip_pretrade_rails.sql`); if `passed = FALSE`, do NOT re-craft — `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('critical','D3','order_guard_block', '<routine> — order guard rejected a staged order: <guard-reasons>; see payload for the order fields', <JSON>)` (`<guard-reasons>` is DISTINCT reason codes, sorted ASCENDING, comma-joined with NO spaces) and leave the row `pending` for next session. If `passed = TRUE`, re-craft a new DAY MARKET instruction for the current session: re-pull `get_price_snapshot` for the live reference price, re-run the ENTER/EXIT-vs-ABANDON judgment (preamble ENTRY/EXIT DECISION — there is no limit to set or chase), `create_order_instruction(contract_id, side, quantity, order_type='MARKET', time_in_force='DAY')` (no `limit_price` argument transmitted), write the updated `ORDER_STAGED` `pending` row (new `payload.instruction_id`, **`guard_passed`/`guard_reasons` from the check just run** — so the daily-staging-cap backstop can recompute the market-only + sanity guard verdict from the payload's own side/qty/ref_price, with no liquidity inputs left to store), and create/repair the 07:00 confirm event. A row whose window has closed unfilled is set terminal `expired` + a missed-order decision logged (do not leave it `pending`) — **but apply the MIS-SET WINDOW CHECK first, exactly as D2a Step 0 branch (c) does (Operating_Protocols.md §11's `entry_window_close` rule binds this path too):** `SELECT * FROM state.staged_order_window_invalid` for that `item_key` (if the view does not exist, treat as NOT listed and proceed with the ordinary expiry). A row listed there was staged at or AFTER the close of the very session its `entry_window_close` names, so it never had a tradable session inside its own window — that is a mis-stamped date, not a window that opened, ran and passed, and expiring it silently downgrades persist-and-wait to abandon-after-one-session. Re-craft it under the same `item_key` with `due_date` `>= state.trading_day_today.next_trading_day` if the intent still stands, or expire it deliberately if it does not, and record which in the decision log. **This clause exists here and not only in D2a because D3 is a genuine alternate path to the same reconciliation** — the same reasoning the ORDER-GUARD CHECK bullet above gives for being restated in this routine. Any legacy or operator-placed GTC still working in `get_account_orders` that is drifted far from the market or past its intended window is flagged for delete/cancel + re-craft to a DAY order rather than left to drift indefinitely.
- Queue hygiene (`state.open_queue` / `events.queue_events`): confirm every open position flagged for research-deferral has a `queue_events` entry (analysis_type: research-deferral-checkpoint) with its resolution `due_date` + `conservative_default`; flag any `state.open_queue` item whose `due_date` is past but still actionable (D2 should have drained it — surface as a missed analysis).
- GO-WITHOUT-ORDER self-check (RUNBOOK §25 D3; covers the registry-centric blind spot). The reconciliations above all walk FROM `state.open_orders`/the connector outward, so a GO that `ops.sp_log_decision` wrote atomically but whose `ORDER_STAGED` row was never written (the session died mid-step) is invisible. Anchor on the decision instead: `SELECT * FROM state.go_without_order` (`bigquery/105_routine_catchup_window.sql`, superseding the original fixed window in `bigquery/18_stack_review_fixes.sql` — GO decisions since GREATEST(36h, D3's own last successful completion) with no matching staged-order row, by `source_decision_ref`/ticker+strategy, AND no fill). For each row, ADJUDICATE (a GO can be analytical or deliberately deferred to a future window — those are fine): if it is a genuine actionable order that should have produced a staged-order/instruction/confirm-event triple and did not, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D3','go_without_order','<ticker>/<strategy> — GO logged <entry_id> but no staged order/fill', '<JSON: entry_id, ticker, strategy>')` (substitute exactly `<ticker>`, `<strategy>`, `<entry_id>` in the fixed sentence, adding nothing; `entry_id` is the stable stranded-GO identity) and re-stage it (craft the order + `ORDER_STAGED` row + confirm event) or, if the window has closed, log the missed-entry decision. **TRADING-ENABLE RE-CHECK — apply BEFORE the re-stage craft:** if the `state.trading_enabled` verdict carried forward from this routine's TRADING-ENABLE GATE reads FALSE, do NOT re-stage — a re-stage creates a NEW `ORDER_STAGED` row, which is new exposure, unlike the persist-and-wait re-craft of an already-staged row above. Still raise the `go_without_order` warning (the detection is the point, and it is not a capital movement), record the deferred re-stage via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` citing `halt_reason`, and let the next D2/D3 run pick it up once the gate clears. Restated inline rather than left to the gate paragraph above, which names this exact site as blocked. A GO that legitimately maps to no order (analysis-only, or a future-dated deferral with its own queue entry) is left alone. **DURABLE ADJUDICATION RECORD — for EVERY row this step reviews, regardless of verdict:** `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` (`events.decision_log`, `entry_type='go-without-order-adjudication'`, citing `entry_id`/ticker/strategy + the verdict: legitimate-no-order / re-staged / missed-and-logged). The window is now anchored to D3's own last successful completion (floored at 36h, never narrower — CATCH-UP EVIDENCE WINDOW, `bigquery/105_routine_catchup_window.sql`), so a GO logged during a multi-day D3 outage stays in-window until D3 next runs instead of silently aging out before ever being reviewed — this makes every adjudication a permanent, queryable fact instead. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D3.md` § H-D3-06.)*

**TRIGGER SELF-REGISTRATION (resilience audit 2026-07-16 — closes OWNER_ACTIONS.md §A autonomously and generalizes it; RemoteTrigger `create` action schema-confirmed).** Compare the routine ids in `ops/cadence.yaml` against the keys of `ops/trigger_ids.json`. For AT MOST ONE routine per D3 run that appears in `ops/cadence.yaml` AND has a canonical instruction entry in `ops/triggers.json` but NO `ops/trigger_ids.json` entry:
1. **IDEMPOTENCY PRECHECK (mandatory — RemoteTrigger `list` pagination is broken per `ops/trigger_ids.json` `_meta`, so `list` can NOT be used to dedup; this decision_log check is the only reliable guard against creating a duplicate live trigger when a prior run's create succeeded but its `ops/trigger_ids.json` commit failed CI):** `SELECT * FROM events.decision_log WHERE entry_type='trigger-self-registration' AND <entry references this routine id>` (any date) — this is the same durable marker OPS0's own STEP 2 item 3 writes/reads when IT is the one self-registering a trigger, so either routine's prior create is visible here. If a row exists, do NOT create — recover the `trig_...` id recorded in that entry (or via `RemoteTrigger get` on it to confirm it is live), write it into `ops/trigger_ids.json` (provenance `'api'`), commit + push, and stop this step for this run.
2. **SLOT LOOKUP, fail-closed:** the schedule comes from the routine's own structured `expected_trigger` block in `ops/cadence.yaml` — read `expected_trigger.cron_utc`, the fixed-UTC cron the live trigger is actually created with (for OPS0: `30 4 * * 1,2,3,4,5` = 04:30 UTC = 10:30 PM MDT / 9:30 PM MST — API-created triggers are fixed-UTC, NOT DST-aware like the native Daily/Weekdays picker, so the slot is pinned in UTC rather than expressed as a plain local time; deliberately kept inside 21:00–24:00 America/Denver year-round because `state.cadence_watch.needs_attention` flips at 21:00 Denver and `state.catchup_available` is same-day-only, bigquery/48_cadence_monitor_unbounded.sql:52-59, and completes before the 05:15 UTC `cadence_check` scheduled-query snapshot). `expected_trigger` is the enforced source of truth (`scripts/check_cadence_consistency.py`), replacing the WEB-UI TRIGGER AUDIT comment block. That block is corroboration for collision/order/DST rationale, never the determinant; report disagreement without reverting precedence. **Fail closed only when NEITHER source carries a slot:** if the routine has no `expected_trigger.cron_utc` AND no line in the audit block, do NOT guess a time: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D3','trigger_slot_unrecorded','<routine> has no live trigger and no schedule recorded in ops/cadence.yaml — neither an expected_trigger.cron_utc nor a WEB-UI TRIGGER AUDIT slot line — record one there first','<JSON: routine>')` and stop. Keep this message template fixed: `sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on an exact message match, so rewording it orphans any open row; change it only when no open row exists.
3. **CREATE:** `RemoteTrigger create` with instruction = the exact `ops/triggers.json` instruction string for the routine and schedule = the recorded slot (a fixed-UTC cron expression per the slot above, not a DST-relative local time). The tool's response appends the server-parsed run time: verify it matches the intended slot; if it does NOT, you MAY call `RemoteTrigger update` on the trigger id returned by THIS run's create (and only that id) to correct it — this is the sole exception to the never-modify rule below.
4. **DURABLE MARKER FIRST, THEN COMMIT:** immediately after a successful create — BEFORE any git operation — `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` (`entry_type='trigger-self-registration'`, body naming routine id + the returned `trig_...` id + the schedule slot). This is the idempotency marker step 1 reads; it must not be deferred past the commit. Then write the `trig_...` id into `ops/trigger_ids.json` (provenance `'api'`), commit + publish through the own-PR protocol (§Branch and state propagation; no human approval step), and `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('info','D3','trigger_self_registered','<routine> live trigger created and id recorded','<JSON: routine, trigger_id, schedule>')`. If the commit/push fails, the decision_log marker guarantees the next D3 run recovers the id via step 1 instead of creating a duplicate.
5. **If the create API call is rejected/unavailable from this session:** `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D3','trigger_create_unsupported','<routine> has no live trigger and the trigger-create API is unavailable from this session — owner must create it per OWNER_ACTIONS.md §A','<JSON: routine>')` and stop (do not retry this run).
NEVER modify or delete any pre-existing trigger in this step (sole exception: step 3's same-run correction of the trigger this run just created); NEVER create a trigger for a routine absent from `ops/triggers.json`; NEVER create more than one trigger per D3 run. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D3.md` § H-D3-07.)*

**OPS0 WATCHDOG-FALLBACK (resilience audit 2026-07-16 — who watches the watcher: OPS0 rides the same trigger platform it guards, and cadence_check's missed_run alert for it is email-only; check corrected 2026-08-08 for the Fri/Sat daily-tier schedule change — see below).** Using `state.trading_day_today.today`, first resolve OPS0's LAST EXPECTED firing day — **not literal calendar-yesterday.** Fri/Sat are skipped; a Sunday check of literal yesterday would falsely flag a scheduled non-fire. Derive the last EXPECTED day from the calendar mechanically instead of hardcoding a day-of-week list:
```sql
SELECT MAX(cal_date) AS ops0_last_expected_day
FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY(DATE_SUB(today, INTERVAL 7 DAY), DATE_SUB(today, INTERVAL 1 DAY))) AS cal_date
WHERE EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM cal_date) NOT IN (6, 7)   -- exclude Friday(6)/Saturday(7); BigQuery DAYOFWEEK 1=Sunday..7=Saturday, same convention as bigquery/09_market_calendar.sql:110
```
then `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='OPS0' AND status='completed' AND run_date = <ops0_last_expected_day>`.  If OPS0 has EVER logged a completed run (self-bootstrapping guard, same convention as `state.cadence_watch.monitored`) AND that count is 0: perform OPS0's STEP 1 and STEP 2 inline, verbatim per that routine's own text (read `state.catchup_refire_readiness`, re-fire each row via `ops/trigger_ids.json` + `RemoteTrigger run`, write the same `ops.catchup_refire_log` rows and per-row alerts — the miss_key idempotency makes this safe even if a delayed OPS0 later runs tonight), with ONE exception: if a row's `routine` is `D3` itself, do NOT call RemoteTrigger (this very session IS the recovery run) — just `INSERT INTO ops.catchup_refire_log (miss_key, routine, tier, outcome, note) VALUES (<miss_key>, 'D3', 'daily', 'refired', 'self-recovered inline — D3 fallback session supersedes')` so the miss_key is closed without spawning a redundant second D3 session. Then `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D3','ops0_missed_fallback','OPS0 did not complete on its last expected day — D3 ran the catchup sweep inline; check OPS0\'s trigger','<JSON: missed_date=ops0_last_expected_day, rows_swept>')`. **CLEAR LIMB — the OTHER branch of the same count, and the ONLY thing that ever closes this category (`bigquery/245_ops0_missed_fallback_policy.sql`).** If that same `COUNT(*)` is **greater than 0** — OPS0 did complete its last expected day — then before moving on, close any notice left over from a previous miss: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved = TRUE, resolved_ts = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note = CONCAT('auto-resolved by D3: OPS0 logged a completed run for its last expected day ', CAST(<ops0_last_expected_day> AS STRING)) WHERE category = 'ops0_missed_fallback' AND NOT resolved` — scope by category here rather than `alert_id` because every open row of this category reports the same single condition (OPS0 is not completing) and that condition has just been measured false; there is no per-row state to preserve. **Do NOT instead age this category out or hand it to `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts`** — an expiring watchdog notice silently discards the one signal that the fleet's own cadence watchdog has stopped running, which is the failure this whole bullet exists to catch. Positive evidence only, and if OPS0's trigger is genuinely broken OPS0 never completes, D3 never sees a count > 0, and the row correctly stays open. The clear limb belongs HERE, not in OPS0: D3 is the independent watcher computing this predicate every run, whereas OPS0 resolving an alert about OPS0 is self-attestation. OPS0's SCOPE GUARDRAIL applies verbatim here: if the readiness view ever emits D2, D2a, M4, Q4, A3, or SL4, STOP and raise a critical instead of re-firing; W4 is queue-only and catchup-safe, so it remains eligible. (Known accepted limitation: this bullet runs after D3's FATAL D2 dependency gate, so a compound day where D2 also missed aborts D3 before this fallback — cadence_check's missed_run email remains that layer's backstop.) *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D3.md` § H-D3-08.)*

Time zone America/Denver unless Experiment_Parameters.md specifies otherwise.

CHAT OUTPUT: one-line summary of calendar + queue reconciliation (e.g., "1 legacy thesis event migrated to queue + deleted; 3 confirm-order events verified; state.open_queue clean (no past-due actionable items).").
```
